evidence.readmeExcerpt:
Automagik

A team of AI helpers that lives in your chats.

Automagik is superintelligence, in open building blocks: a team of AI agents in your chats,
and each part usable on its own once it ships; Cloud is still in design.

The film: our own GTM team. The team launching Automagik, at work. Music only, no voice-over.
Watch the film on automagik.si

⬇ Download for Mac  ·  ⬇ Download for Linux

Cloud is coming; no date yet. Join the Cloud waitlist on automagik.si

This repository, Genie and Omni are free and open source, Apache-2.0. Cloud is a private, paid service.
Mac with Apple silicon, macOS 13 or newer · Linux on a 64-bit PC · Windows is not supported yet

--- ## Two modes **Team mode** is the desktop app: a team of long-lived Bots, each with its own name, role, model and memory. They talk to you, to each other and in group chats, run scheduled tasks, and each drives a browser of its own. With an [Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) connected, your WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and other channels sit in the same window, and the Bot you put on a chat acts when something happens there. The team runs on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). **Code mode** is your code agents in the real [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) window, with the Automagik pack: a sidebar of spaces, Bots and workers across coding harnesses. Nothing in Herdr is rebuilt. The app's switch brings the Herdr window forward on the space for the current Bot's folder, and a button in Herdr brings you back. The app download alone does not set Code mode up: it needs Herdr and the pack, and [the pack's installer](herdr/README.md#install) sets up both. Team mode: the app's switch still says Work. ## The seven blocks Each block is usable alone. - **[Team mode (DSH)](apps/bots-dsh/README.md)**: the Bot team on DeepSeek Harness: long-lived Bots with their own name, role, model and memory, group chats, schedules and the Bot browser. - **[Code mode (Herdr)](herdr/README.md)**: your code agents in the real Herdr window with the Automagik pack; nothing in Herdr is rebuilt. - **[Genie](https://github.com/automagik-si/genie)**: a wish becomes a branch, a test run and a report you approve; `genie desktop` opens it on the team. - **[Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni)**: the service that links your chat apps to Automagik, with its channels and canvases in the same window. - **[Pocket](apps/pocket/README.md)**: your coding agents on your Android phone, paired to your own machines. - **[The meter](meter/usagemeter/README.md)**: usagemeter, the Rust token meter that records usage and cost on the machine and answers `usagemeter query`. - **[Cloud](docs/rfcs/0024-automagik-cloud.md)**: one sign-in, organisations and hosted workspaces, with a rail that opens each. Cloud is designed and accepted, and is not live. When it ships it is a private, paid hosted service: not free and not open source. Only its contracts are public (RFC 0024). ## What makes it yours - **Your model.** Connect the AI account you already have, or an API key from a provider you use. Each Bot runs on the model you give it. - **Your files and memory, on your computer.** What the team keeps is in one folder, `.automagik` in your home folder. Each Bot keeps notes across its conversations, each group chat keeps its own, and the team shares one more. Your chats stay in your Omni. What your Bots read and write goes to the AI account you connected, under that company's terms. - **Secrets the Bots never see.** When a Bot needs an API key, a token or a password, it asks with a card in its own chat. You type the value; the Bot never sees it. - **It asks before it acts as you.** Before a Bot sends a message as you to a person, deletes something or disconnects a channel, it shows you exactly what it will do and asks first. The exceptions: your Main Bot and an Omni Bot read your chats and post to a group, a WhatsApp channel or your own chat with yourself without asking. Any other Bot reads and posts only where you allow: the first time it wants a chat it asks, and you answer **Once**, **Always** or **No**; after **Always** it posts to that group without asking again. ## Install The current release is always at [Releases](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest). **Mac** (Apple silicon, macOS 13 or newer): 1. [Download Automagik for Mac](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Mac.dmg). 2. Open **Automagik-Mac.dmg** and drag the Automagik icon onto the Applications folder. 3. Open **Automagik** from Applications. **Linux** (64-bit PC): 1. [Download Automagik for Linux (.deb)](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Linux.deb) for Ubuntu or Debian. 2. Double-click it and choose **Install**, or run `sudo apt install ./Automagik-Linux.deb`. 3. Open **Automagik** from your apps. On another Linux, use the [AppImage](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Linux.AppImage). Windows is not supported yet. The app has two things to connect when you are ready: an Omni and an AI account. Both can wait. The full guide, updates, your data and uninstall are in [apps/desktop](apps/desktop/README.md). Code mode installs separately: [herdr](herdr/README.md#install). Pocket: [apps/pocket](apps/pocket/README.md#install). am alone on a host without the Herdr app (install, verify, update, roll back): [am/README.md](am/README.md). **For your code agent**: `npx skills add automagik-si/automagik --skill am` adds the skill that teaches it `am`, Automagik's one command. ## This repository Automagik's plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), and the Automagik desktop app that runs them, with the Herdr pack (`herdr/`), Pocket (`apps/pocket/`) and the meter (`meter/`). | Folder | Package | What it is | |---|---|---| | [`apps/bots-dsh`](apps/bots-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/bots-dsh` | The Bot team: long-lived Bots, group chats, memory, settings, scheduled tasks, the Bot browser. Omni's and Genie's plugins build on it. | | [`apps/welcome-dsh`](apps/welcome-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/welcome-dsh` | The welcome: the octopus, the team step, and Connect AI through DSH's own sign-ins. | | [`apps/acp-dsh`](apps/acp-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/acp-dsh` | Agents other than DSH's own, over ACP (Agent Client Protocol), as DSH models: the agent's tool calls show as DSH tool cards and ask through DSH's approval dialog (RFC 0003). | | [`apps/locale-pt-br-dsh`](apps/locale-pt-br-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh` | Português: the Bot team's Brazilian Portuguese under DSH's own Portuguese entry. Adds no language of its own, so Settings › General › Language keeps one Portuguese row; a pt-BR choice saved by an older pack moves to DSH's pt. | | [`apps/multiuser-dsh`](apps/multiuser-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/multiuser-dsh` | Server-side caller admission and attribution for gated workspaces (RFC 0038). | | [`apps/vault-dsh`](apps/vault-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/vault-dsh` | Bitwarden fields for approved Bot commands, with unlock and mapping in Settings › Secrets (RFC 0034). | | [`apps/desktop`](apps/desktop/README.md) | (the app) | The Automagik desktop app: DSH of its own with the Bot team, the welcome and Omni's channels and canvases. `omni desktop` opens it with Omni preloaded, `genie desktop` with Genie. | Omni's own plugins (its channels and canvases) live with Omni, in [automagik-si/omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) (`apps/omni-channels-dsh`, `apps/omni-canvas-dsh`), and carry Omni's version. ### Install into your own DSH - **The desktop app**: download it from [Releases](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest), or run `omni desktop`. See [apps/desktop](apps/desktop/README.md). - **Into your own DSH**: add the Automagik market to DSH's plugin market and install from there: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/automagik-si/dsh-marketplace/main/index.json ``` Every Omni also serves a market at `https:///api/market/index.json` with the release of these plugins it was tested with. Nothing here is published to npm. The plugins install as git sources pinned to a release commit, or from the tarballs each release carries (`plugins.json` lists their integrity). ### History `@automagik/bots-dsh` and `@automagik/welcome-dsh` were `@automagik/omni-dsh` and `@automagik/omni-ai-dsh` in automagik-dev/omni (`apps/omni-ui-dsh`, `apps/omni-ai-dsh`), and the desktop app was automagik-dev/omni-desktop. They moved here with their history. What did not change with the names: plugin ids (`omni-ui`, `omni-ai`), routes and browser-storage prefixes. From 3.12 the team's home is Automagik's own (`~/.automagik/bots`, or `~/.automagik/desktop/bots` in the app), and the app's identity is Automagik's (`ai.namastex.automagik`): an app from 3.11.x or before is installed afresh, not updated. - The Bot team's client bundle also answers to its former name, so channels and canvas plugins built before the rename keep working on it. - In your own DSH: install `@automagik/bots-dsh` from the market. With both installed, the newer one runs (they share the plugin id); remove `@automagik/omni-dsh` when you like. A settings row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` that names `@automagik/omni-dsh` needs its `name:` changed to `@automagik/bots-dsh` to keep applying. ### Versions and releases One version for the whole repository, `3.N` (semver `3.N.0`, N one above the last release: `scripts/version.ts`), above the 2.x builds omni-desktop released. Every merge into dev is a release: `release.yml` tags `v`, publishes the plugin tarballs and `plugins.json`, builds the desktop app into the same release (`desktop-build.yml`), lists the release in [`marketplace/automagik.json`](marketplace/automagik.json), and moves `main` to it. `follow-omni.yml` moves the desktop app to each newer Omni release and cuts a release with it. | Branch | What | |---|---| | `dev` | Integration: pull requests land here; releases are cut from it | | `main` | The latest release, moved by `release.yml` only | ### Develop Bun for the repository's own tooling; the plugins run on Node, as DSH does (`node --test`, esbuild), with Bun installing them; the desktop app uses npm for Electron. ```sh bun install && bun run check # versions, release tooling, market index cd apps/bots-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test cd apps/welcome-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test cd apps/desktop && npm ci && npm test node scripts/boot-check.mjs # boot the plugins with Omni's in headless Chromium ``` ### License This repository is Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). [Genie](https://github.com/automagik-si/genie) and [Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) are Apache-2.0 in their own repositories. Automagik Cloud is not part of this licence: it is a private, paid service.

# @automagik/bots-dsh

Omni for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh): a team of long-lived Bots that talk to you, to each other and in group chats, with Omni as the Main Bot. With the Omni channels plugin, Omni also operates your Omni channels, chats and automations inside dsh; with the Omni canvas plugin, it shows what it found as live views in the chat (see [Three plugins](#three-plugins)). It is built on [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot) (Apache-2.0, see `VENDORED.md`).

> Labs release. Features, tools and the saved data format can still change.

The dsh versions it supports are the range in `engines.dsh` in its [`package.json`](package.json); dsh checks that range and does not load the plugin on a version outside it.

**Your own dsh stays yours.** Installed into an existing dsh, the team keeps its files in `$AUTOMAGIK_HOME/bots` (`~/.automagik/bots`), keeps the key of the Omni it is linked to in its own file there, uses its own route (`/api/omni-ui`), plugin id (`omni-ui`) and browser-storage prefix (`omni-ui:`), overrides no other plugin's configuration, and checks for no updates. It can run beside upstream DS Bot.

## Three plugins

Omni for dsh is three packages. This one is the team; the other two sit on it and add Omni's own parts. Install all three to have everything; the team works alone.

| Package | Folder | Row id | What it adds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@automagik/bots-dsh` (this one) | `apps/bots-dsh` | `omni-ui` | The Bot team and its surface: Bots, group chats, settings, themes, interface copy, memory, secrets, usage, scheduled tasks, the Bot browser, updates, diagnostics, the `POST /api/omni-ui` route, and the `web-search` plugin |
| `@automagik/omni-channels-dsh` | [`apps/omni-channels-dsh` in Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni/tree/dev/apps/omni-channels-dsh#readme) | `omni-channels` | The link to an Omni (pairing, `omni.json`), the Channels page and chats, Omni's tools for the platform (and the shell and file tools a Main Bot loses for them), the events Omni listens to, automations and their board, Omni's operator rules, and the onboarding step Connect Omni (`omni-connect`) |
| `@automagik/omni-canvas-dsh` | [`apps/omni-canvas-dsh` in Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni/tree/dev/apps/omni-canvas-dsh#readme) | `omni-canvas` | `show_canvas`, the canvas check, the canvas language in Omni's rules, and the renderer that draws canvases in the chat (OpenUI and zod live only here) |

How they fit:

- **Host**: this plugin provides its runtime as the `omniTeam` service. The channels plugin injects it, installs its modules on a runtime whose prototype is the team's, and provides that one as `omniChannels`; the canvas plugin injects both and sits on the channels runtime. Each plugin's tools, listeners and effects stay on its own fiber, and it adds to the team only through `rt.hooks` (`src/host/extend.js`): `endpoint(name, fn, { read })` for the `/api/omni-ui` route, `view(fn)` and `live(fn)` for the state answers, `sessionOwner(fn)` for the team Bot and optional label of an external run Session, and `mainRules(fn, { order })` for a part of the Main Bot's rules, which stay inside the one `bot-identity` section. A plugin that runs a Bot kind on its own engine, not on a DSH model, owns that kind's model menu with `botModels(kind, { snapshot, pick, refresh })` (`src/host/host-models.js` has the shape): the team then never selects a DSH model for those Bots (their settings and `list_bots` name what the plugin says answers), their menu lists only the plugin's entries (each with where a message goes, the one picked and the one answering now) and levels, and only you pick; a Bot's `update_bot` with a model or level is refused. Without a registration the team answers as before. Each hook returns its disposer, so turning a plugin off takes what it added with it. Five more parts of the runtime are for other plugins:
  - `rt.resumable.register({ id, sessions, onResume })` hands the team's one restart pass (`src/host/resume.js`) the plain Sessions a plugin owns: `sessions()` names them when the pass runs, `onResume({ sessionId })` runs right before the team posts a resume to one of them (whoever found it), and the registration returns its disposer. Every resume post carries `source.resumed === true`.
  - `rt.resumesDone` is one promise per start that never rejects: `{ resumed, resent }` after the pass, `{ readOnly, resumed: [], resent: [] }` on a host that only reads the team, `{ failed, resumed, resent }` when it threw or stopped. `resumed` lists every Session the pass resumed, `resent` every Session it sent dropped messages again.
  - `rt.noteStop(sessionId, { why, tool, callId, text })` notes a permission stop for the person; `rt.teamOwnerOf(sessionId, agent)` resolves the team Bot and place, including a subagent's parent. Plugins can feature-detect both. Reasons are `never`, `unavailable`, `tool`, `level`, `address`, `review`, `sandbox` and `rule`; external grants and guards use `rule`.
  - `rt.dshBots`: `list()` gives `[{ id, name, workDir, profile }]` (`null`: the team workspace, DSH's default preset), `createSession(botId, { title, firstMessage })` gives `{ sessionId }` in that DSH bot's folder with its preset, and `onChange(fn)` calls `fn(list)` when the list changes and returns its disposer.
  - `rt.mountCapability(sessionId, name, grant)` and `rt.unmountCapability(sessionId, name)` mount one MCP capability into one plain Session the plugin owns, and only there ([A capability for one Session](#a-capability-for-one-session)).
- **Browser**: this plugin's `client.js` exports `omni`: the host call, the interface copy (`t`, `addStrings`), the Bot surface's registries (`toolCards`, `nav`, `badges`, `botChildren`, `headerButtons`, `sidebarTools`, `botSettings`, `onShell`, `setCanvasRenderer`, `registerComposerPack`), the running surface (`face`) and a few UI pieces (`ui`). The other plugins name `@automagik/bots-dsh/client` in `dsh.client.external`, so dsh loads this bundle first and hands them the same module instance: one dictionary, one roster, one set of registries.
- **Composer**: a Bot's composer changes with the model it runs on (`src/client/composer-packs.js`). Every Bot's chat shows the model that Bot runs on in its own model menu, which saves to that Bot alone: with thinking levels when the model has them, and on an agent over ACP (`acp-claude`, `acp-codex`) with the levels the agent offers for that model, or without any when it offers none. On a Bot whose plugin owns its model menu, it shows that menu. A group chat, where each member runs on its own model, and a Bot still waiting for its model show none. The plan cell and the activity and usage docks stay Omni's in every pack. Other plugins add a pack with `omni.registerComposerPack({ id, order, match(provider, target), available(env), cells: { permission, model }, hostFor })`.
- **Data**: all three keep the team's one `state.json` and its lock (automations ride it); `omni.json` is the channels plugin's, in the same folder.
- **Upgrading from one package**: a team linked to an Omni whose dsh has only this plugin shows a card in the sidebar footer that points to the plugin market for the channels plugin.

## Features

- **Long-lived Bots**: each Bot is a dsh Session in the "DS Bot" workspace, with its own name, role, instructions and model.
- **Working folders**: a Bot can work in a folder you choose instead of the team workspace, and a group chat can set one folder for all its members there. Pick it in the Bot's settings or details panel or in the group's settings, or ask a Bot (`update_bot`, `update_group`). After a change, the chat goes on in a fresh part that starts in the new folder. When a Bot sets a folder outside the team workspace, or adds a Bot to a group that works in one, it asks for your approval if those Bots can only write in their folder. Folders that hold dsh data (`$DSH_HOME`, the team's data) are refused. The team workspace itself moves in Settings > General > Locations; Bots and groups that work there go on in a fresh part in the new folder, and the old folder keeps its files.
- **Folder for these four file tools**: open **File-tool folder** by the composer of a root Session to set or clear its folder for `read`, `read_image`, `glob` and `grep`. The owner’s choice is saved for that Session, takes effect on the next call and survives reopening it. A fresh conversation you start has its own setting. A continuation, a delegated task and a native subagent use their initiating root’s setting. A scoped call needs an explicit existing absolute path whose real path stays inside the folder. The tools refuse `..`, dangling links and links that resolve outside. Scoped searches skip links encountered during traversal and ignore ripgrep configuration and ignore files. Shell, ACP readers and file previews have their own permissions.

  The desktop and server profiles bind the four DSH `0.2.2-rc.2` tool definitions to their local filesystem or subprocess provider. A scoped call refuses a tool or provider the profile cannot verify. DSH’s `FileSystem` and `SubprocessRuntime.spawn` APIs carry no per-Session read root. Enforcement across providers or against concurrent filesystem changes during an OS open requires provider-side support. DSH’s `appendPluginRecord` is reserved for its own experimental packages, so Automagik stores the choice and delegated bindings in `session-read-scopes/` in its team home.

  DSH’s scheduler exposes a reserved `new_once` Session ID in `ScheduleService.catalog()`. Its `schedule/resolve-agent` hook takes a destination Session ID, and the catalog omits the pending destination of a recurring `new` task. A fresh delivery whose initiating root could be scoped is held when that root cannot be identified. A scheduled Session created from ambiguous candidates also refuses the four tools if any of those roots later takes a folder.

- **Permission presets**: each Bot runs with its own dsh permission preset (Read only, Workspace or Full access), set in its details panel. A group chat can run all its members with one preset there, in place of their own: turn on **Same for every member** under Permissions in the group's settings. A new Bot starts with the team default, set under Permissions in Settings > Bots. Work a Bot opens never runs wider than the conversation that opens it. A task (`start_task`, a Genie wish) runs at the narrower of its own level and the level that conversation runs at when it starts it, such as a chat lowered with `/permission` or a read-only automation run. A Bot made with `create_bot` starts at the narrowest of its creator's level, that conversation's and its group's, and never gets a tool its creator does not have. A fresh Session a Bot's scheduled task opens starts no wider than that Bot. While a task you scheduled yourself also opens fresh Sessions, DeepSeek Harness does not say which task a fresh Session is for, so those keep the level they start with. A level that cannot be read or compared gives the narrowest one offered. What you start yourself is as before. While DSH's experimental Auto review plugin is on, **Auto review** is a preset too, marked Experimental and confirmed once when picked. Where Auto cannot hold (the plugin is off, or DSH refuses it), the Bot or group runs as Workspace and says so; a chat whose Session was left on Auto opens again once Auto review is back on. When DSH stops offering a saved level (an upgrade renames or drops it), the level stays saved and is not rewritten: a conversation that already runs is lowered to the narrowest level DSH still offers when that is known to allow less than what it has, and is otherwise left as it is; nothing new starts (a task, a greeting, a first turn in a group) until a level is picked or DSH offers the saved one again. Details and Settings → Feedback say which of these happened. Only you set permissions; Bots cannot change them.

  Auto works as Workspace on every supported route. Codex uses its own reviewer. Claude Code is withheld from Auto until its `auto` mode is captured; a saved Claude Code Auto mark is cleared and the Bot runs as Workspace. API Bots use their own model in a separate request for sandbox escalations; a granted step can leave the sandbox. Hermes, Antigravity and omp use the team's background model and are offered Auto only while one is available. Their own tools run outside DSH's sandbox.
  For bridged Codex in Auto, the team's background model decides DSH tool calls. If the CLI asks for permission, the rest of that prompt's bridge calls reach the person. Without a background model, bridge calls reach the person. Hard-to-undo steps and the rest of a turn after three consecutive refusals or ten total refusals always reach the person when Automagik judges. Plugin, folder and website approvals remain with the person. A request the judge decides never shows as a card, on the computer or on Pocket; only one it passes on does. A model failure asks; it never allows. Only the person turns Auto on. API marks bind the exact model; native agent marks bind their route. Bots outside Auto keep their existing behavior.

  **Auto** is Workspace plus a saved mark, chosen only by you after a confirmation in Details,
  the composer menu or the chat's permission card; the question names who decides for that Bot.
  Every message reaching the Bot's current chat counts, including another Bot's or a schedule's.
  Auto needs Workspace in the Session and this host holding the team;
  otherwise the saved choice says **Runs as Workspace here**. Picking any level, Workspace again
  included, ends Auto and its agent sessions; route and model changes clear it too.
  Deny lists coexist with Auto: changing one keeps the mark, moves the permission revision
  and ends agent sessions and outstanding grants. DSH refuses native/API and bridged denied
  calls whatever the judge says. Unbridged CLI built-ins and team agents’ own tools were
  never covered at Workspace either; they need to use DSH’s bridge for the deny to reach them.
  Tasks and Bots opened from that chat while Auto counts there inherit it; an inherited task
  counts only while the opener's mark and permission revision match. Groups, Settings and the
  team default offer no Auto row.
- **Permission stops**: a stopped step shows in the sidebar and Live rail, beside its tool call or in its group round, and on a working task card. Stops outside the visible conversation get a system notification where notifications are already allowed; a child or late group stop also notifies when that conversation cannot draw it. Pocket shows an English hint at the end of an own-chat turn. Stops live in memory and are lost on restart. The first stop per reason and turn also adds one diagnostics line in Settings → Feedback. A refusal nobody answered tells the Bot so, Auto review's final denial gives its reason, a subagent's unasked refusals reach its parent, and a coding CLI's held turn answers in the interface language.
- **Subagents**: in-process children of Read only, Workspace and Auto review Bots keep that level with approval prompts on, without changing their captured sandbox. Their asks appear above the composer of the Bot's chat or task (open it from the task card), or in the group member card; the sidebar, Live rail and notifications also show that they wait. Children keep DSH's refusal, shown as a permission stop, when their Bot runs at Full access, with approval prompts off, or at a custom or unknown level; when the Bot's level changed while the child was being created; when a resumed child has its prompts off; and when they belong to an automation run, a plugin Session, an earlier part or an ended task. An ask nothing here can answer is cancelled and noted as a stop. The phone does not show child asks.
- **Hard steps and repeated refusals**: at Read only, Workspace and DSH Auto review,
  recursive deletes, force pushes, remote branch deletes, hard resets and cleans,
  infrastructure destroys, database drops, file-tool deletes and deleting a Bot or group,
  secret files/token commands, external messages, shared or ambiguous pushes, and deletes
  outside the Bot’s folder ask the person when the existing tool gate allows them. Children follow the same check.
  Read-only team lookups such as `recall` do not ask just because their arguments mention a hard step.
  Auto also asks about these steps inside its Workspace boundary; its judge keeps its own counts.
  Plugins classify external senders through `rt.stepHooks.sendsOutside(fn)`; a failed hook asks.
  Ordinary example env files, public SSH keys, feature-branch pushes with an explicit
  destination and local file deletes stay out of the added list; a bare `git push` or a
  destination of `HEAD` asks. Exact boundaries are in RFC 0031’s #1092 amendment.
  The judge’s deadline covers model lookup too; grants bind arguments. `rt.autoAuditRows()`
  exposes its last 200 decisions without arguments, including allows, outside the failures list.
  After three consecutive automatic refusals or ten in a turn, the next refusal asks
  “Let it keep working?” Allow once only lets work continue: nothing refused runs.
  Reject stops the Bot for that turn. If approvals are off or no chat, group seat or working
  task can show the question, work stops with a reason and an automatic-stop notification
  when that host hook is available. Full access is unchanged.
  Unbridged Claude Code gets session-only ask rules for expressible hard steps at every
  asking level, removed by restarting its session across Full access. These rules include
  password-manager reads. Bridged Claude has no Bash of its own: its DSH calls use the checks
  above. Codex's own tools are excluded:
  prompt rules under its Full access `never` policy refuse instead of asking, rules have no
  per-session path, and its `agent` mode sends prompt rules to its reviewer, not the person.
  This is an unmet dependency: Codex built-ins run without `session/request_permission`.
  Enforcing the list needs a mandatory per-session ask policy before its reviewer or a blocking
  pre-execution request with tool, arguments and cwd. Claude wildcard rules cannot express
  outside-folder deletes or ambiguous push targets either; those need a bridge or richer policy.

- **Bots work together**: `message_bot` sends a message to another Bot, `create_bot`, `update_bot` and `delete_bot` add, set up and remove Bots (including a profile photo from a local image file or a data URL), and `ask_user` asks you a question without blocking the other Bots. `show_view` draws a card in a Bot's own chat — text, metrics, tables, progress, choices, confirmations and short forms; an interactive card waits for your answer.
- **Group chats**: members speak one at a time, and each one reads the latest messages first. A message can `@Name` a member to pass the turn on; type `@` to pick one from a list. **+ → Reference a chat** adds another Bot's chat to a message as context, and in a group the members who answer get it. A member with nothing new to add stays quiet (`[PASS]`). Each member has its own hidden Session per group, so a group never reads a Bot's private chat.
- **Roles and permissions**:

  | Who | Can do |
  |---|---|
  | You | Everything |
  | Main Bot (there can be more than one) | Manage every group; change and delete Bots |
  | Group admin | Manage its own group only (name, notice, members, reply mode) |
  | Member | Speak in the group, `@` another member, and post into its groups from outside them |

- **Shell access**: each Bot either has a shell or does not. Every new Bot states its
  capability; a new private-folder Bot states off, and a Bot saved before it existed has
  no field and reads as a shell, with no migration. Only the user changes the switch in
  its settings. A Bot without a shell gets no `bash`, `pwsh` or terminal tool,
  and no tool that runs a command or starts one for it: a DSH task (`start_task`), an ACP
  agent's execute call (`acp_tool`; its reads and edits stay), a local CLI's command
  approval (`approve_agent_action`), an MCP server that would start a command
  (`save_capability`, `attach_capability`) and the computer-use tools (`cua`,
  `cua_driver_native__*`). The rule holds on the Bot's own chat, a group Session, a task, a
  subagent (delegation stays, its child is bound to the parent's fence), a renamed or
  aliased tool, and a skill. It is enforced where DSH grants tools — the tools are removed,
  not forbidden by an instruction — and not with an operating-system sandbox. A Bot with
  shell access can read what the operating-system user can read: that is the honest limit
  of the folder fence for shell commands.

  A shell-less Bot cannot be paired with a model whose agent runs its own tools: the Bot
  team refuses it at creation, at the model pick, at a route switch and at the Remote
  Hermes pairing, both when the shell is switched off and when the agent is set. The
  automatic move of a Bot off a retired plan route to its coding CLI skips a shell-less
  Bot, keeps it where it is and says once why (the CLI brings its own shell); if that plan
  route no longer answers, the Bot asks for a model instead of looking like it works. An
  MCP server mounted before the shell was turned off keeps running, but a command tool it
  exposes is refused; a server mounted after the switch is refused too. The settings card
  says what this capability does not fence: another Bot with a shell, or the
  operating-system user, can still read files this Bot can read.
- **Scheduled tasks and restricted Bots**: a Bot with a deny list or no shell cannot create
  or edit a scheduled task, because a `new` or `new_once` target opens a Session no deny
  layer binds; the tasks it already armed are paused and their record stays. A
  delivery no team lineage can bind is refused while such a task cannot be paused;
  when the pause lands, dsh is asked to drive again and the refused delivery goes
  through. A reminder due during the boot window, before the team has loaded, is
  refused the same way and lands once the team loads.
- **Long chats stay inside the model's window**: dsh's own compaction never runs on a Bot's Session. When a turn ends past the check line (a share of the model's context window), a small separate model call, the context steward, reads the latest messages of the chat and decides once. If the work is still under way, the chat is condensed in place into a checkpoint: a handoff summary plus your recent messages word for word. If the work has reached a stopping point, the Bot writes a handoff note and continues in a new part. Either way you still see one chat, with no marker. Earlier parts and condensed messages stay searchable in a full-text index (`node:sqlite` FTS5) through `read_own_chat`. These side calls (steward, note, checkpoint) never go to an agent over ACP (Claude Code, Codex): they run on the team's background model, and a Bot with no model that answers beside its agent skips them, says so once in the log, and past the hard line continues in a new part that carries its latest messages word for word, without a model call. Switching a Bot from an agent to an API model measures the chat against that model's own switch threshold (computed as DSH's compaction does) before DSH checks it: below it nothing happens; above it, the chat is condensed into a checkpoint only when you picked a background model in Settings and the chat fits that model (it is the one charged), and otherwise the Bot continues in a new part with the latest messages that fit, no note and no model call. The part it leaves is archived only once the new part's first answer comes from the chosen model; if that first call fails, the Bot goes back to the part it left. No message is deleted either way.
- **Memory**: each Bot keeps notes across all its conversations, each group chat keeps its own for its members, and the team shares one more. See [Memory](#memory).
- **Web search**: see [Web search](#web-search).
- **Bot browser**: each Bot drives a browser of its own: it opens pages, clicks, types, uploads and downloads. Posting, uploading, downloading and deleting ask you first, and payments always come back to you. See [Bot browser](#bot-browser).
- **Side chat**: ask a Bot about its work while it runs, in the side panel (`/side`, or `/btw` as before), without stopping its turn or adding to its chat. Nothing runs to answer.
- **Images**: for a model that cannot read images, a vision model first turns the image into text.
- **Secrets**: a Bot asks for an API key or token with a card in its own chat and never sees the value. See [Secrets](#secrets).
- **Usage**: Settings → Usage shows token usage by time (24 hours to 12 months, or days picked on a calendar), by Bot and by model, with a page for each Bot and each model. Calls that a Session logs are read from the logs, so older chats count too. Calls that leave no log (checkpoints, handoff notes, the steward, image readings, dsh titles and compaction) are counted while they stream, from the time the plugin runs. Legacy aggregates can omit provider fields; they do not claim a cross-provider cache percentage. Tokens only, no cost.
- **Official right sidebar**: every Bot chat can open Live as a tab in DSH's own pane, rather than a second fixed rail. DSH owns its collapse, focus, docking and narrow-screen behavior. Existing Browser, side-chat and plugin routes remain available.
- **Advanced Bot**: Bot Settings has a per-Bot switch, initially off and saved across parts and restarts. It reveals supported native session controls, Context and Stats without changing identity, permissions, model access or context policy. Models and permissions remain managed by the canonical Bot controls. Ordinary DSH keeps its native conversation surface.
- **Advanced Context**: shows current part/checkpoint boundaries, measured or estimated usage and effective usable/check/hard windows. Per-Bot check threshold and recent-message carry budget override host defaults (80% and 16,384 tokens); the 95% hard safety threshold is protected and effective carry is additionally capped by the check line. **Checkpoint now** requires an idle, loaded own-chat Session and condenses that same Session through Bot maintenance; stale, running, cancelled or read-only requests fail rather than bypass the native guard. **Start new part** is separate, confirmed and carries nothing from the old part. Native manual Bot compaction remains unavailable, with an explanation. Automatic memory review has separate own-chat controls/status and no guaranteed ordering with compaction; a host-wide off setting cannot be overridden.
- **Advanced Stats**: read-only last-request, last-turn, current-Session and Bot-total scopes show input/output/cache read/cache write, logical calls, recorded attempts and retries where reported. Session drilldown is limited to that Bot's own-chat parts; Bot totals partition group, task/child and tagged memory/steward/checkpoint/handoff overhead without adding overlapping scopes together. Unlinked overhead is not guessed into a request or turn. Missing is **Unknown**, not zero; legacy provenance cannot be reconstructed. Cache ratios are token-weighted within compatible, explicitly identified provider normalization, with their prompt-token denominator displayed; providers are never averaged together. Refresh may update the derived ledger but never runs a model or changes a Session. Partial history is labeled. No cost, timing, task-success or native-DSH effectiveness comparison is inferred.
- **DSH bots**: New… → New DSH bot creates a native DSH identity with a name, project folder and preset, and immediately adds team membership: the native DSH conversation UI and tooling stay available alongside roster, messages, groups and browser access. It has the same final shape as adopting an existing DSH bot, with one sidebar row and a retained original registration. Membership failure fails creation and cleans up the new registration and Session. If archival or required persistence is unavailable, a durable pending-creation registration retains ownership and tool restrictions, stays hidden from both rosters, and retries cleanup on the next load (including restart). The error reports pending cleanup; it never reports successful standalone creation. Cleanup waits for an operation-bound terminal receipt in `agent-creations/<UUID>.json`, published atomically by the allocation's producer only after native creation settles—even if that producer lost the team lock or was disposed. This receipt contains only operation and Session IDs plus outcome, grants no team-write or archival authority, and is removed after durable membership or cleanup. Missing/invalid receipts (including a hard kill before publication or receipt persistence failure) retain hidden pending ownership rather than guessing that an absent Session cannot appear later; back up `agent-creations/` with the team file while creation is pending. Cleanup is claimed durably before archival so an old producer cannot re-adopt an archived Session. DSH archival and the team file are not atomic: a failed post-archive save can temporarily retain a pending reference to an archived Session, which idempotent retry removes. For compatibility, legacy `add-agent` callers without `teamMember: true` and `rt.dshBots` keep the standalone DSH registration/session contract (no team tools); the UI explicitly opts into membership. A Bot's one-off work (`start_task`) runs under that Bot and reports back when its first turn ends.
- **Adopting a DSH bot**: **Adopt as Bot** adds team membership without replacing the DSH identity, native conversation surface, preset, avatar or capabilities. The newest Session becomes its team chat and earlier Sessions remain readable parts; nothing is renamed or recreated. `list_bots`, messages, groups, capabilities and tasks be

# Português (`@automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh`) Brazilian Portuguese for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH 0.2.2 ships Portuguese itself, as **Português** (`pt`); this client plugin adds the part DSH does not carry — the Bot team's own `omni-ui` strings — under that same entry. It adds no language: Settings › General › Language keeps exactly **one** Portuguese row, DSH's. Supported runtime: **DSH 0.2.2-rc.2 or later** (`engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.2-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`). Earlier DSH series have no `pt` to register under; this pack requires rc.2 or later. ## One Portuguese entry The pack used to add its own **Português (Brasil)** entry with a corrected copy of four DSH namespaces (date order, thousands separator, the plan hint and several mistranslations). A pack cannot override a namespace DSH already registers for `pt` — the second registration throws (`locale namespace "" already has locale "pt"`) — so those corrections required a second language, and therefore a second Portuguese row in the picker. That row is gone. The Language list shows DSH's **Português** alone, and DSH's `pt` copy serves the DSH screens. The pack's own strings are the Bot team's, and they belong to the Bot team's namespace: DSH does not have `omni-ui`. ## What it carries | Namespace | Keys | Why | |---|---|---| | `omni-ui` | all | The Bot team's namespace (`@automagik/bots-dsh`), which DSH does not have; registered under `pt` | `omni-ui` holds every Bot team key. A few keep their English text on purpose: brand and product names (`Omni`, `DSH`, `Automagik`, `DeepSeek`, `Claude`, `Codex`, `ChatGPT`, `OpenAI`, `Anthropic`, `Google`, `GitHub`, `Namastex`, `Kimi`, `WeChat`, `WeCom`, `DingTalk`, `Feishu`, `MCP`, `API`), code-like strings (`cookies.txt, JSON, storageState`, `MEMORY.md`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `~/.codex/pets`, `#rrggbb`, `@Name`, `/side`, `/feedback`), words Brazilian Portuguese uses unchanged (`Chat`, `Bots`, `Plugins`, `Admin`, `Site`, `Terminal`, `Endpoint`, `Feedback`, `Skill`, `status`, `tokens`, `Pets`, `Chats`, `Design`, `Beta`, `Cc`), and strings that are only a value (`{count}`, `{n}h`, `1 item`, `{percent}%`, `{label}: {version}`). `test/coverage.test.js` requires every Bot key to have an entry and at least 95% of them to differ from the English text. A plugin from outside this repository can add its own words to `omni-ui` through the Bot team's `addStrings`. `scripts/copy-check.mjs` lists in `OMNI_PLUGIN_STRINGS` a recorded fixture of the keys each one adds (their English text), under `test/fixtures/`: today `unfold-session-strings.json`, the model-menu messages of Unfold's session plugin, recorded at the hand-over commit when it left with the Unfold plugins (RFC 0020). Those keys are checked and covered like the Bot team's. The Bot team words a host message with any language pack's entry for it. The welcome (`@automagik/welcome-dsh`) keeps its own copy in its `welcome.team` namespace and registers it under DSH's `pt` as well, so the onboarding reads in Portuguese with this pack installed. ## Upgrading from the old pack, and removing it A profile that installed the pack before 0.2.2 has an older copy that registered a **pt-BR** language and its dictionaries. DSH replaces a plugin in place: when it loads this version it unloads the old one first, whose language and dictionary effects are disposed with it. This client adds no language at all, so it cannot leave a second Portuguese row behind; while the old copy is still mounted, it does not register over the dictionary the old copy holds (it waits for that copy's disposer), so nothing throws on a duplicate locale registration. A language choice saved as `pt-BR` under the old pack is an exact id to DSH's locale runtime, and DSH's entry is `pt`. On load the pack rewrites the stored choice through the runtime's only preference write (`setLocale`), before the choice is read, so a team that picked **Português (Brasil)** opens in Portuguese instead of falling back to English. A browser or home that never picked a language is left alone. To stop shipping the Bot team's strings, remove the plugin: `dsh plugin --profile remove @automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh` (or Settings › Plugins, then the Plugins page, which manages what the list only shows). DSH's own **Português** entry and everything DSH translates stay; only `omni-ui` falls back to its English text, and a saved `pt` choice keeps resolving. ## Install 1. Add the Automagik market to DSH's plugin market ([marketplace/README.md](../../marketplace/README.md) has the URL). 2. Install **Português (Brasil)** — the market title of this pack. If DSH asks for a restart, restart it. 3. Pick **Português** in Settings › General › Language (DSH's entry), or open DSH in a browser set to Portuguese. The client declares `inject: ['locale']` and loads in DSH's first boot phase (`immediately`). The host half does nothing. It needs no settings. ## Develop ```sh bun run harness # the pinned DSH release the tests and the linter run against bun run build # client.js from src/client; commit it with the sources bun run test # on Node: a fake locale service, then DSH's own LocaleRuntime bun run lint node scripts/copy-check.mjs # every pt-BR text against its English text and the copy rules ``` `src/client/locales/pt-BR/omni-ui.json` is keyed by the Bot team's English text. The copy check rejects a key the Bot team no longer has and every `{placeholder}` that does not match its English text. Its rules: Brazilian Portuguese, gender-neutral for the person, no article before Unfold, "clique" for a click, and "ambiente isolado" for a sandbox.

Cloud is coming; no date yet. Join the Cloud waitlist on automagik.si

This repository, Genie and Omni are free and open source, Apache-2.0. Cloud is a private, paid service.
Mac with Apple silicon, macOS 13 or newer · Linux on a 64-bit PC · Windows is not supported yet

--- ## Two modes **Team mode** is the desktop app: a team of long-lived Bots, each with its own name, role, model and memory. They talk to you, to each other and in group chats, run scheduled tasks, and each drives a browser of its own. With an [Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) connected, your WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and other channels sit in the same window, and the Bot you put on a chat acts when something happens there. The team runs on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). **Code mode** is your code agents in the real [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) window, with the Automagik pack: a sidebar of spaces, Bots and workers across coding harnesses. Nothing in Herdr is rebuilt. The app's switch brings the Herdr window forward on the space for the current Bot's folder, and a button in Herdr brings you back. The app download alone does not set Code mode up: it needs Herdr and the pack, and [the pack's installer](herdr/README.md#install) sets up both. Team mode: the app's switch still says Work. ## The seven blocks Each block is usable alone. - **[Team mode (DSH)](apps/bots-dsh/README.md)**: the Bot team on DeepSeek Harness: long-lived Bots with their own name, role, model and memory, group chats, schedules and the Bot browser. - **[Code mode (Herdr)](herdr/README.md)**: your code agents in the real Herdr window with the Automagik pack; nothing in Herdr is rebuilt. - **[Genie](https://github.com/automagik-si/genie)**: a wish becomes a branch, a test run and a report you approve; `genie desktop` opens it on the team. - **[Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni)**: the service that links your chat apps to Automagik, with its channels and canvases in the same window. - **[Pocket](apps/pocket/README.md)**: your coding agents on your Android phone, paired to your own machines. - **[The meter](meter/usagemeter/README.md)**: usagemeter, the Rust token meter that records usage and cost on the machine and answers `usagemeter query`. - **[Cloud](docs/rfcs/0024-automagik-cloud.md)**: one sign-in, organisations and hosted workspaces, with a rail that opens each. Cloud is designed and accepted, and is not live. When it ships it is a private, paid hosted service: not free and not open source. Only its contracts are public (RFC 0024). ## What makes it yours - **Your model.** Connect the AI account you already have, or an API key from a provider you use. Each Bot runs on the model you give it. - **Your files and memory, on your computer.** What the team keeps is in one folder, `.automagik` in your home folder. Each Bot keeps notes across its conversations, each group chat keeps its own, and the team shares one more. Your chats stay in your Omni. What your Bots read and write goes to the AI account you connected, under that company's terms. - **Secrets the Bots never see.** When a Bot needs an API key, a token or a password, it asks with a card in its own chat. You type the value; the Bot never sees it. - **It asks before it acts as you.** Before a Bot sends a message as you to a person, deletes something or disconnects a channel, it shows you exactly what it will do and asks first. The exceptions: your Main Bot and an Omni Bot read your chats and post to a group, a WhatsApp channel or your own chat with yourself without asking. Any other Bot reads and posts only where you allow: the first time it wants a chat it asks, and you answer **Once**, **Always** or **No**; after **Always** it posts to that group without asking again. ## Install The current release is always at [Releases](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest). **Mac** (Apple silicon, macOS 13 or newer): 1. [Download Automagik for Mac](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Mac.dmg). 2. Open **Automagik-Mac.dmg** and drag the Automagik icon onto the Applications folder. 3. Open **Automagik** from Applications. **Linux** (64-bit PC): 1. [Download Automagik for Linux (.deb)](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Linux.deb) for Ubuntu or Debian. 2. Double-click it and choose **Install**, or run `sudo apt install ./Automagik-Linux.deb`. 3. Open **Automagik** from your apps. On another Linux, use the [AppImage](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Linux.AppImage). Windows is not supported yet. The app has two things to connect when you are ready: an Omni and an AI account. Both can wait. The full guide, updates, your data and uninstall are in [apps/desktop](apps/desktop/README.md). Code mode installs separately: [herdr](herdr/README.md#install). Pocket: [apps/pocket](apps/pocket/README.md#install). am alone on a host without the Herdr app (install, verify, update, roll back): [am/README.md](am/README.md). **For your code agent**: `npx skills add automagik-si/automagik --skill am` adds the skill that teaches it `am`, Automagik's one command. ## This repository Automagik's plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), and the Automagik desktop app that runs them, with the Herdr pack (`herdr/`), Pocket (`apps/pocket/`) and the meter (`meter/`). | Folder | Package | What it is | |---|---|---| | [`apps/bots-dsh`](apps/bots-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/bots-dsh` | The Bot team: long-lived Bots, group chats, memory, settings, scheduled tasks, the Bot browser. Omni's and Genie's plugins build on it. | | [`apps/welcome-dsh`](apps/welcome-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/welcome-dsh` | The welcome: the octopus, the team step, and Connect AI through DSH's own sign-ins. | | [`apps/acp-dsh`](apps/acp-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/acp-dsh` | Agents other than DSH's own, over ACP (Agent Client Protocol), as DSH models: the agent's tool calls show as DSH tool cards and ask through DSH's approval dialog (RFC 0003). | | [`apps/locale-pt-br-dsh`](apps/locale-pt-br-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh` | Português: the Bot team's Brazilian Portuguese under DSH's own Portuguese entry. Adds no language of its own, so Settings › General › Language keeps one Portuguese row; a pt-BR choice saved by an older pack moves to DSH's pt. | | [`apps/multiuser-dsh`](apps/multiuser-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/multiuser-dsh` | Server-side caller admission and attribution for gated workspaces (RFC 0038). | | [`apps/vault-dsh`](apps/vault-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/vault-dsh` | Bitwarden fields for approved Bot commands, with unlock and mapping in Settings › Secrets (RFC 0034). | | [`apps/desktop`](apps/desktop/README.md) | (the app) | The Automagik desktop app: DSH of its own with the Bot team, the welcome and Omni's channels and canvases. `omni desktop` opens it with Omni preloaded, `genie desktop` with Genie. | Omni's own plugins (its channels and canvases) live with Omni, in [automagik-si/omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) (`apps/omni-channels-dsh`, `apps/omni-canvas-dsh`), and carry Omni's version. ### Install into your own DSH - **The desktop app**: download it from [Releases](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest), or run `omni desktop`. See [apps/desktop](apps/desktop/README.md). - **Into your own DSH**: add the Automagik market to DSH's plugin market and install from there: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/automagik-si/dsh-marketplace/main/index.json ``` Every Omni also serves a market at `https:///api/market/index.json` with the release of these plugins it was tested with. Nothing here is published to npm. The plugins install as git sources pinned to a release commit, or from the tarballs each release carries (`plugins.json` lists their integrity). ### History `@automagik/bots-dsh` and `@automagik/welcome-dsh` were `@automagik/omni-dsh` and `@automagik/omni-ai-dsh` in automagik-dev/omni (`apps/omni-ui-dsh`, `apps/omni-ai-dsh`), and the desktop app was automagik-dev/omni-desktop. They moved here with their history. What did not change with the names: plugin ids (`omni-ui`, `omni-ai`), routes and browser-storage prefixes. From 3.12 the team's home is Automagik's own (`~/.automagik/bots`, or `~/.automagik/desktop/bots` in the app), and the app's identity is Automagik's (`ai.namastex.automagik`): an app from 3.11.x or before is installed afresh, not updated. - The Bot team's client bundle also answers to its former name, so channels and canvas plugins built before the rename keep working on it. - In your own DSH: install `@automagik/bots-dsh` from the market. With both installed, the newer one runs (they share the plugin id); remove `@automagik/omni-dsh` when you like. A settings row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` that names `@automagik/omni-dsh` needs its `name:` changed to `@automagik/bots-dsh` to keep applying. ### Versions and releases One version for the whole repository, `3.N` (semver `3.N.0`, N one above the last release: `scripts/version.ts`), above the 2.x builds omni-desktop released. Every merge into dev is a release: `release.yml` tags `v`, publishes the plugin tarballs and `plugins.json`, builds the desktop app into the same release (`desktop-build.yml`), lists the release in [`marketplace/automagik.json`](marketplace/automagik.json), and moves `main` to it. `follow-omni.yml` moves the desktop app to each newer Omni release and cuts a release with it. | Branch | What | |---|---| | `dev` | Integration: pull requests land here; releases are cut from it | | `main` | The latest release, moved by `release.yml` only | ### Develop Bun for the repository's own tooling; the plugins run on Node, as DSH does (`node --test`, esbuild), with Bun installing them; the desktop app uses npm for Electron. ```sh bun install && bun run check # versions, release tooling, market index cd apps/bots-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test cd apps/welcome-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test cd apps/desktop && npm ci && npm test node scripts/boot-check.mjs # boot the plugins with Omni's in headless Chromium ``` ### License This repository is Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). [Genie](https://github.com/automagik-si/genie) and [Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) are Apache-2.0 in their own repositories. Automagik Cloud is not part of this licence: it is a private, paid service.

# Vault for DeepSeek Harness Install and enable `@automagik/vault-dsh` from the Automagik market. Install Bitwarden CLI 2026.10.1 or a later 2026.10 patch separately and sign in on the host. For Vaultwarden or a self-hosted Bitwarden server, set the server with `bw config server` before signing in. Use a CLI account with a master password. Password login and API key login both work when the account can unlock with its master password. Key Connector and SSO accounts without a master password cannot unlock through this plugin. In the Bot team's Settings › Secrets, unlock the vault and use **Add a vault key** to map an item field and choose which Bots may ask for it. Each use requires approval of the exact shell command. The plugin supports login username, login password, notes and unique hidden or text custom fields. Read access covers a single configured CLI account. The master password goes to the unlock child through its environment. The plugin keeps the returned session key in memory and locks after the configured idle time (`idleLockMinutes`, 5 minutes by default, from the last unlock or successful read). **Lock**, disabling the plugin and a planned desktop quit drop the key and lock an owned session. Bitwarden CLI manages its own account and local vault data. Each approved read forces a sync before retrieving the selected field. The exact network failures in [RFC 0034](../../docs/rfcs/0034-vault-plugin-bitwarden-first.md) permit a stale read from the CLI's local vault. Other sync failures refuse the read and lock the session. ## 1Password service accounts Install 1Password CLI 2.39.0 or a later 2.x version on the host. Give a service account read access to the vaults it needs. In local Settings › Secrets, select **1Password** under **Vault** and enter the service account token. The picker groups items by vault and identifies fields with duplicate labels by section. The token lives in plugin memory and is passed through the environment of authenticated `op` children. Every authenticated command disables the CLI cache. **Clear token**, idle lock, disabling the plugin and quitting clear the token. Enter it again after restarting. If the CLI cannot read the current value, the request is refused. 1Password service accounts are available on hosts where `op` runs, except Automagik Cloud. The team uses a single vault provider and connection. Remove the existing mappings before switching. Before rolling back to an older Bot team plugin, remove 1Password mappings so the older host can read the mapping file. Delivery 2b covers shell delivery. ## HashiCorp Vault KV Install a stable Vault CLI 2.0, 2.1 or 2.2 release. In local Settings › Secrets › Vault, select **HashiCorp Vault** and enter the server address, token and optional namespace. Use HTTPS. HTTP is available for loopback at `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` or `localhost`. Automagik Cloud does not support this provider. Other OS keychain providers are deferred. Enter a KV v1 or v2 mount to browse its folders and choose a field. The plugin checks the exact mount before each item read or listing. The token needs access to that mount preflight and the relevant read and list paths. With no mapping, connect tries the mount table and tolerates a policy denial there. Values are read fresh and field selection happens inside the adapter. Use the Vault server directly or a non-caching Vault Proxy that forwards the supplied token. Caching Vault Proxies are unsupported and cannot be detected. HTTPS uses the OS trust store. Forward proxies, custom CAs and redirects are unsupported. The endpoint and token live in memory until lock, idle expiry, a provider switch, disable or quit. Each authenticated CLI child receives them through its environment. The plugin gives each child an isolated home and removes its empty private directory after the child exits. Vault paths appear in transient CLI arguments and may appear in Vault's own audit. Same-user processes can inspect a running CLI's arguments and environment. Automagik saves the reference and a hash of the canonical endpoint and namespace in `vault-sources.json`. Reconnect to the same endpoint and namespace after a restart to use those mappings. A different endpoint or namespace invalidates pending approvals and grants. Remove the HashiCorp Vault mappings before rolling back to an older Bot team plugin. To check the transport against a local copy of the Vault CLI, set `VAULT_REAL_BIN` to the binary and run `hashicorp-vault-cli.test.js`. The test uses an in-process loopback responder. ## Secret Service (GNOME Keyring) On Linux, select **Secret Service (GNOME Keyring)** in local Settings › Secrets › Vault and choose **Unlock**. This opens Automagik’s access without a password. Manage the actual keyring lock in GNOME. The picker shows locked collections without their items. Select an item from an unlocked collection and save the mapping. An item can still lock after the plugin gate opens. Automagik Cloud, KeePassXC and KWallet are outside this delivery. The gate monitors the session bus and its Secret Service owner. An owner change, a bus disconnect or change of identity, **Lock**, idle expiry, a provider switch, disable or quit closes the gate and invalidates approvals. A successful field read renews the same idle timer. Reference changes require a new mapping. Before rolling back to a Bot team version that predates this provider, remove all Secret Service mappings. ### Product choices - The owner’s process name, executable basename and PID start time check compatibility with GNOME Keyring. This trusts the person’s desktop bus and the backing store GNOME opens. Same-user processes are inside that trust boundary. - The saved reference is the canonical item path, exact creation time and the first 32 hex characters of SHA-256 over the sorted attribute pairs. The path can contain a collection name. It is stored in `vault-sources.json`. Picker handles expire with the listing or gate. The plugin fetches attributes for a selection when saving it. The unkeyed digest can confirm guesses about predictable attributes. - The reference detects changes before and after each read. Secret Service has no atomic conditional read. A replacement may enter the adapter’s memory, then be erased and refused if the post-check detects a change. A restored item with the same path, creation time and attributes is treated as the same item. - Values use the DH-AES encrypted session. Labels and attributes are ordinary D-Bus property replies outside that session. Access uses the explicitly supplied session bus address, via one Unix endpoint. Closing the plugin gate leaves the desktop keyring’s OS permissions and lock state as they were. - Reads accept `text/plain` in fatal UTF-8, preserving whitespace and a BOM and refusing NUL. A wire byte array is limited to 64 KiB. The Bot team applies its existing secret-value rules. The required private-keyring acceptance test is `VAULT_SS_REAL=1 node --import ./test/harness-resolve.mjs --test test/secret-service-real.test.js`. Run it with Node 24.9 and the extracted AppImage runtime with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`. It requires a private Unix socket, `dbus-daemon`, `gnome-keyring-daemon` and `/usr/bin/python3` with the D-Bus and libsecret bindings. ## Proton Pass Install Proton Pass CLI 2.7.1 and create a personal access token with read access to a vault. In local Settings › Secrets › Vault › Proton Pass, choose **Set token**. The token is used once to sign in and is dropped after login. The CLI keeps its encrypted session in a private temporary folder with a memory-only key. On Windows the folder relies on the per-user temporary directory's access controls. **Lock**, idle lock, a provider switch, disabling the plugin and quitting remove the session. The plugin also locks at most 110 minutes after login starts, before Proton's two-hour session expiry. Enter the token again after the vault locks. The picker lists items shared through a vault, and only built-in fields can be mapped. Custom fields and grants for individually shared items are unsupported. Agent tokens are unsupported. The adapter supplies no reason, so the CLI refuses reads for sessions it classifies as agent sessions. A token the CLI classifies as an ordinary personal access token reads like one. Proton may record reads in its Business read report. Forward proxies are unsupported. Proton Pass is unavailable in Automagik Cloud. ## Bitwarden Secrets Manager machine accounts Install `bws` 2.x on the host. In local Settings › Secrets › Vault, choose **Bitwarden Secrets Manager**, enter the server (`us`, `eu`, or a self-hosted HTTPS base URL) and select **Set token**. Use a machine account scoped to the projects it needs. The picker lists projects first and lets you choose a project's keys. The token is saved in the host user's keychain. After a restart or lock, select **Unlock** to activate it again. **Clear token** deletes the saved credential and locks the adapter. Settings sends the displayed connection label with Clear. A provider-only request requires an active Secrets Manager connection or a mapping to identify the saved item. Setting a fresh token for the same connection replaces its saved server and token. The adapter confirms the saved record before activating the replacement. With two DSH processes on one profile, a Clear in one does not end the other's in-memory session. That session ends at its idle lock, an explicit lock, or quit. Remote and Pocket clients cannot change or unlock the credential. Cloud support is deferred. With `bws` 2.1.0, HTTP 401 and HTTP 400 with an `invalid_client` or `invalid_grant` error lock the adapter. The CLI reports identity and item API errors in the same format, so D4c classifies a 404 from `bws secret get` as unavailable and leaves the adapter unlocked. The adapter never classifies a `bws` diagnostic as revoked. macOS uses the login keychain's default ACL, which trusts `/usr/bin/security`. A same-user process can use that executable to read the credential while the login keychain is unlocked, including between CLI calls. Removing that trust would require prompting on reads. Linux and WSL use the local login session's Secret Service through `secret-tool`. Windows uses the current user's Credential Manager. Before rolling back, remove Bitwarden Secrets Manager mappings and clear the saved token while this version is still installed. Older Bot team versions reject the mapping file when it contains a Bitwarden Secrets Manager row. The host-only `secretSources` v1 service provides `status`, `unlock`, `lock`, `read`, `listItems` and `prepareQuit`. The `providers` property lists supported providers. HashiCorp Vault also exposes `listFields` for the host picker. Secret Service exposes `resolveHandle` and `itemDetail` for the host and `providerBinding` for gate generation checks. `status()` defaults to Bitwarden, and `status({ provider })` checks the named provider. Run `bun run harness` to install the pinned test harness and `bun run test` to run the fake-CLI tests.

Automagik

A team of AI helpers that lives in your chats.

Automagik is superintelligence, in open building blocks: a team of AI agents in your chats,
and each part usable on its own once it ships; Cloud is still in design.

The film: our own GTM team. The team launching Automagik, at work. Music only, no voice-over.
Watch the film on automagik.si

⬇ Download for Mac  ·  ⬇ Download for Linux

Cloud is coming; no date yet. Join the Cloud waitlist on automagik.si

This repository, Genie and Omni are free and open source, Apache-2.0. Cloud is a private, paid service.
Mac with Apple silicon, macOS 13 or newer · Linux on a 64-bit PC · Windows is not supported yet

--- ## Two modes **Team mode** is the desktop app: a team of long-lived Bots, each with its own name, role, model and memory. They talk to you, to each other and in group chats, run scheduled tasks, and each drives a browser of its own. With an [Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) connected, your WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and other channels sit in the same window, and the Bot you put on a chat acts when something happens there. The team runs on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). **Code mode** is your code agents in the real [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) window, with the Automagik pack: a sidebar of spaces, Bots and workers across coding harnesses. Nothing in Herdr is rebuilt. The app's switch brings the Herdr window forward on the space for the current Bot's folder, and a button in Herdr brings you back. The app download alone does not set Code mode up: it needs Herdr and the pack, and [the pack's installer](herdr/README.md#install) sets up both. Team mode: the app's switch still says Work. ## The seven blocks Each block is usable alone. - **[Team mode (DSH)](apps/bots-dsh/README.md)**: the Bot team on DeepSeek Harness: long-lived Bots with their own name, role, model and memory, group chats, schedules and the Bot browser. - **[Code mode (Herdr)](herdr/README.md)**: your code agents in the real Herdr window with the Automagik pack; nothing in Herdr is rebuilt. - **[Genie](https://github.com/automagik-si/genie)**: a wish becomes a branch, a test run and a report you approve; `genie desktop` opens it on the team. - **[Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni)**: the service that links your chat apps to Automagik, with its channels and canvases in the same window. - **[Pocket](apps/pocket/README.md)**: your coding agents on your Android phone, paired to your own machines. - **[The meter](meter/usagemeter/README.md)**: usagemeter, the Rust token meter that records usage and cost on the machine and answers `usagemeter query`. - **[Cloud](docs/rfcs/0024-automagik-cloud.md)**: one sign-in, organisations and hosted workspaces, with a rail that opens each. Cloud is designed and accepted, and is not live. When it ships it is a private, paid hosted service: not free and not open source. Only its contracts are public (RFC 0024). ## What makes it yours - **Your model.** Connect the AI account you already have, or an API key from a provider you use. Each Bot runs on the model you give it. - **Your files and memory, on your computer.** What the team keeps is in one folder, `.automagik` in your home folder. Each Bot keeps notes across its conversations, each group chat keeps its own, and the team shares one more. Your chats stay in your Omni. What your Bots read and write goes to the AI account you connected, under that company's terms. - **Secrets the Bots never see.** When a Bot needs an API key, a token or a password, it asks with a card in its own chat. You type the value; the Bot never sees it. - **It asks before it acts as you.** Before a Bot sends a message as you to a person, deletes something or disconnects a channel, it shows you exactly what it will do and asks first. The exceptions: your Main Bot and an Omni Bot read your chats and post to a group, a WhatsApp channel or your own chat with yourself without asking. Any other Bot reads and posts only where you allow: the first time it wants a chat it asks, and you answer **Once**, **Always** or **No**; after **Always** it posts to that group without asking again. ## Install The current release is always at [Releases](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest). **Mac** (Apple silicon, macOS 13 or newer): 1. [Download Automagik for Mac](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Mac.dmg). 2. Open **Automagik-Mac.dmg** and drag the Automagik icon onto the Applications folder. 3. Open **Automagik** from Applications. **Linux** (64-bit PC): 1. [Download Automagik for Linux (.deb)](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Linux.deb) for Ubuntu or Debian. 2. Double-click it and choose **Install**, or run `sudo apt install ./Automagik-Linux.deb`. 3. Open **Automagik** from your apps. On another Linux, use the [AppImage](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Linux.AppImage). Windows is not supported yet. The app has two things to connect when you are ready: an Omni and an AI account. Both can wait. The full guide, updates, your data and uninstall are in [apps/desktop](apps/desktop/README.md). Code mode installs separately: [herdr](herdr/README.md#install). Pocket: [apps/pocket](apps/pocket/README.md#install). am alone on a host without the Herdr app (install, verify, update, roll back): [am/README.md](am/README.md). **For your code agent**: `npx skills add automagik-si/automagik --skill am` adds the skill that teaches it `am`, Automagik's one command. ## This repository Automagik's plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), and the Automagik desktop app that runs them, with the Herdr pack (`herdr/`), Pocket (`apps/pocket/`) and the meter (`meter/`). | Folder | Package | What it is | |---|---|---| | [`apps/bots-dsh`](apps/bots-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/bots-dsh` | The Bot team: long-lived Bots, group chats, memory, settings, scheduled tasks, the Bot browser. Omni's and Genie's plugins build on it. | | [`apps/welcome-dsh`](apps/welcome-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/welcome-dsh` | The welcome: the octopus, the team step, and Connect AI through DSH's own sign-ins. | | [`apps/acp-dsh`](apps/acp-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/acp-dsh` | Agents other than DSH's own, over ACP (Agent Client Protocol), as DSH models: the agent's tool calls show as DSH tool cards and ask through DSH's approval dialog (RFC 0003). | | [`apps/locale-pt-br-dsh`](apps/locale-pt-br-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh` | Português: the Bot team's Brazilian Portuguese under DSH's own Portuguese entry. Adds no language of its own, so Settings › General › Language keeps one Portuguese row; a pt-BR choice saved by an older pack moves to DSH's pt. | | [`apps/multiuser-dsh`](apps/multiuser-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/multiuser-dsh` | Server-side caller admission and attribution for gated workspaces (RFC 0038). | | [`apps/vault-dsh`](apps/vault-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/vault-dsh` | Bitwarden fields for approved Bot commands, with unlock and mapping in Settings › Secrets (RFC 0034). | | [`apps/desktop`](apps/desktop/README.md) | (the app) | The Automagik desktop app: DSH of its own with the Bot team, the welcome and Omni's channels and canvases. `omni desktop` opens it with Omni preloaded, `genie desktop` with Genie. | Omni's own plugins (its channels and canvases) live with Omni, in [automagik-si/omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) (`apps/omni-channels-dsh`, `apps/omni-canvas-dsh`), and carry Omni's version. ### Install into your own DSH - **The desktop app**: download it from [Releases](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest), or run `omni desktop`. See [apps/desktop](apps/desktop/README.md). - **Into your own DSH**: add the Automagik market to DSH's plugin market and install from there: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/automagik-si/dsh-marketplace/main/index.json ``` Every Omni also serves a market at `https:///api/market/index.json` with the release of these plugins it was tested with. Nothing here is published to npm. The plugins install as git sources pinned to a release commit, or from the tarballs each release carries (`plugins.json` lists their integrity). ### History `@automagik/bots-dsh` and `@automagik/welcome-dsh` were `@automagik/omni-dsh` and `@automagik/omni-ai-dsh` in automagik-dev/omni (`apps/omni-ui-dsh`, `apps/omni-ai-dsh`), and the desktop app was automagik-dev/omni-desktop. They moved here with their history. What did not change with the names: plugin ids (`omni-ui`, `omni-ai`), routes and browser-storage prefixes. From 3.12 the team's home is Automagik's own (`~/.automagik/bots`, or `~/.automagik/desktop/bots` in the app), and the app's identity is Automagik's (`ai.namastex.automagik`): an app from 3.11.x or before is installed afresh, not updated. - The Bot team's client bundle also answers to its former name, so channels and canvas plugins built before the rename keep working on it. - In your own DSH: install `@automagik/bots-dsh` from the market. With both installed, the newer one runs (they share the plugin id); remove `@automagik/omni-dsh` when you like. A settings row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` that names `@automagik/omni-dsh` needs its `name:` changed to `@automagik/bots-dsh` to keep applying. ### Versions and releases One version for the whole repository, `3.N` (semver `3.N.0`, N one above the last release: `scripts/version.ts`), above the 2.x builds omni-desktop released. Every merge into dev is a release: `release.yml` tags `v`, publishes the plugin tarballs and `plugins.json`, builds the desktop app into the same release (`desktop-build.yml`), lists the release in [`marketplace/automagik.json`](marketplace/automagik.json), and moves `main` to it. `follow-omni.yml` moves the desktop app to each newer Omni release and cuts a release with it. | Branch | What | |---|---| | `dev` | Integration: pull requests land here; releases are cut from it | | `main` | The latest release, moved by `release.yml` only | ### Develop Bun for the repository's own tooling; the plugins run on Node, as DSH does (`node --test`, esbuild), with Bun installing them; the desktop app uses npm for Electron. ```sh bun install && bun run check # versions, release tooling, market index cd apps/bots-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test cd apps/welcome-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test cd apps/desktop && npm ci && npm test node scripts/boot-check.mjs # boot the plugins with Omni's in headless Chromium ``` ### License This repository is Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). [Genie](https://github.com/automagik-si/genie) and [Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) are Apache-2.0 in their own repositories. Automagik Cloud is not part of this licence: it is a private, paid service.
