# revit-tools

> Query a live Revit 2027 model through an AI chat — no cloud, no API keys, one file.
> **Experimental proof of concept. Not production software.**

---

## What it is

`revit-tools` is a single-file, standard-library-only Python MCP server that bridges an AI assistant to a running Revit 2027 model. It spawns Autodesk's official `Autodesk.RevitMcpServer.Stdio.exe` as a child process and adds a deterministic audit suite on top.

**15 MCP tools:**
- **7 native Autodesk tools** — `query_model`, `get_element_data`, `export_views` (schedules to CSV), `open_view`, `select_elements`, `zoom_to_elements`, `get_running_revit_instances`
- **8 deterministic audit tools** — floor area, lot area (shoelace formula), lot coverage, septic, energy, WWR, setback. Pure math, no LLM guesswork.

**Key properties:**
- **Read-only and fully local.** Nothing is written to the model. No data leaves the machine.
- **Deterministic math.** The audit tools compute numbers from the model's geometry. When data is absent, the tool says "not in the model" instead of inventing a figure.
- **Auto-discovers the running Revit instance.** Detects the first process ID and injects `revitInstanceId` into every call so the agent doesn't have to manage it by hand.
- **Zero external dependencies.** Python standard library only — no `pip install`, no `requirements.txt`, no `.env`, no pywin32.

---

## Prerequisites

- **Windows** (the Revit MCP add-in runs on Windows only)
- **Revit 2027** with the [**Revit MCP Server Read-Tools Technical Preview**](https://www.autodesk.com/) add-in installed, a model open
- **Python 3.9 or later** (any CPython — the server is stdlib-only)
- An **MCP client** — either [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek.com/) (DSH) or any other stdio MCP client (Claude Desktop, Continue, etc.)

---

## Installation

### Option A: DeepSeek Harness (preset)

The `revit-tools` folder is a self-contained DSH preset. Copy it to your DSH agent-presets directory:

```powershell
# Copy the entire folder to your DSH presets
copy .\revit-tools\ %USERPROFILE%\.dsh\.agent-presets\revit-tools\
```

Then edit `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\.agent-presets\revit-tools\agent.cordis.yml` and fix **three paths**:

```yaml
- id: mcp-revit-tools
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
  config:
    serverName: revit-tools
    transport: stdio
    command: 'python'   # <-- the target machine's Python (or full path)
    cwd: '<PRESET-FOLDER-PATH>'   # <-- where you copied the folder
    args:
      - 'axo_mcp_server.py'
      - '<EXE-PATH>'   # <-- path to Autodesk.RevitMcpServer.Stdio.exe
    toolCallTimeoutMs: 300000
```

The Autodesk exe is installed at:

```
C:\Program Files\Autodesk\Revit 2027 MCP Server Read-Tools Technical Preview\Autodesk.RevitMcpServer.Stdio.exe
```

Start a new DSH session on the **Revit Tools** preset. The 15 tools will appear as `mcp__revit_tools__*`.

### Option B: Any MCP client (standalone)

If you use a different MCP client (Claude Desktop, Continue, Cursor, etc.), point it directly at the server:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "revit-tools": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": [
        "path/to/axo_mcp_server.py",
        "path/to/Autodesk.RevitMcpServer.Stdio.exe"
      ],
      "cwd": "path/to/preset-folder"
    }
  }
}
```

The server runs on standard I/O — no network ports, no firewall changes.

---

## How to use

Once your MCP client has discovered the tools, ask in plain English:

| You say | What runs |
|---|---|
| "Total floor area per level" | `axo_audit_floor_area` |
| "What's the lot area and building lot coverage?" | `axo_audit_lot_area` + `axo_audit_lot_coverage` |
| "Export the door and window schedules to CSV" | `get_running_revit_instances` → `export_views` |
| "Window-to-wall ratio, septic clearances, energy envelope" | `axo_audit_wwr`, `axo_audit_septic`, `axo_audit_energy` |
| "List all walls on level 1 with dimensions" | `query_model`(OST_Walls) → `get_element_data` |
| "Which Revit documents are open?" | `get_running_revit_instances` |

Explicit tool names (DSH): `mcp__revit_tools__query_model`, `mcp__revit_tools__axo_audit_floor_area`, etc.

---

## Available tools

### Native Autodesk (pass-through)

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `get_running_revit_instances` | Lists open Revit processes with active/linked documents |
| `query_model` | Query elements by category, returns element IDs |
| `get_element_data` | Retrieve detailed parameters for given element IDs |
| `export_views` | Export schedules to CSV file |
| `open_view` | Navigate to a view in Revit |
| `select_elements` | Highlight elements in the Revit UI |
| `zoom_to_elements` | Focus the camera on selected elements |

### Axoworks audit tools (deterministic)

| Tool | What it computes |
|---|---|
| `axo_audit_floor_area` | Room-based floor area by level, with optional level filter |
| `axo_query_floor_area` | OST_Floors element areas; maximum single-level plate = building footprint |
| `axo_audit_lot_area` | Lot area from OST_SiteProperty via shoelace formula; sq ft and acres |
| `axo_audit_lot_coverage` | Building footprint ÷ lot area × 100 (composite of the two above) |
| `axo_audit_septic` | Counts plumbing fixtures and property lines (distances pending add-in update) |
| `axo_audit_energy` | Energy envelope stub (placeholder — parity with original engine) |
| `axo_audit_wwr` | Window-to-wall ratio count (area ratio pending add-in geometry) |
| `axo_audit_setback` | Setback distance stub (property-line geometry not exported by add-in) |

> Audit tools marked "placeholder" return honest narratives about what they could and could not compute. They never invent a number.

---

## Architecture

```
MCP client (DSH, Claude Desktop, etc.)
  │
  └─ stdio ──▶ axo_mcp_server.py  (one file, Python stdlib only)
                  │
                  ├─ child stdio ──▶ Autodesk.RevitMcpServer.Stdio.exe
                  │                     │
                  │                     └─ named pipe ──▶ MCP add-in inside Revit 2027
                  │
                  └─ adds the 8 axo_* audit tools (deterministic math over native surface)
```

The server serializes all upstream calls, applies per-call timeouts, and auto-injects the `revitInstanceId` parameter.

---

## Limitations

These come from the Autodesk Revit MCP Server 2027 Technical Preview and apply to any client built on it:

1. **Single-threaded.** Every query queues on Revit's UI thread. Rapid-fire calls or retry loops can **permanently deadlock** the MCP connection (symptom: `tools/list` answers, `query_model` hangs forever). The only cure is restarting the add-in or Revit. **One query at a time, stop on error, never retry-storm.**
2. **Read-only, host model only.** Linked models are visible in `get_running_revit_instances` but cannot be queried.
3. **`searchScope` discipline.** Always pass `"searchScope": "AllViews"` in `query_model` — the server defaults to the active view and returns empty lists otherwise.
4. **`OST_Roofs` can hang.** On complex models, test with `maxResults: 1` before larger roof queries.
5. **Geometry not fully exposed.** Property-line geometry is not exported, so setback distances and true window-to-wall area ratios are not derivable. Energy U-factor/SHGC extraction is also a placeholder. These are honest "unavailable" narratives, not errors.
6. **Heavy queries are slow.** 30–60+ seconds for large extractions is normal. Budget a generous tool timeout (5 minutes in the default config).
7. **No governance layer.** The server serializes calls and applies timeouts, but does not deduplicate, heartbeat, or re-audit payloads. The *agent* must be disciplined: stop on error, do not retry blindly.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause / fix |
|---|---|
| No tools appear in session | MCP client not connected to the server. Verify the `command` and `args` paths. |
| `tools/list` OK but all queries hang | Main-thread deadlock (limitation #1). Restart the MCP add-in or Revit. |
| `get_running_revit_instances` → `[]` | Pipe attach in flight. The add-in connects ~2–3 seconds after first contact; call it again. |
| `query_model` returns empty `{ "levels": [] }` | Missing `"searchScope": "AllViews"` in the call. |
| Audit tools report "no rooms" / "0 sq ft" | Data gap in the model (rooms not placed, Area unpopulated), not a connection problem. |
| Tool call times out | Complex model; budget 5 minutes. Do **not** loop-retry (limitation #1). |

---

## Comparison with other routes

Two other configurations exist on the same machine for reference:

- **`revit` (proxy):** The original Axoworks middleware — Python proxy with governance, coordinate translation, and the same audit suite. Requires the `revitmcp` repo, venv, and pip dependencies.
- **`revit-direct` (bare):** Launches the Autodesk exe directly. Zero Python, 7 native tools, no audit suite. No instance auto-injection — the agent must manage `revitInstanceId` manually.

All three use distinct `serverName` values and can coexist in the same DSH process without collision.

---

# dsh-02x

Custom agent presets for **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x**, one installable bundle per subdirectory.

**Tested on DSH `0.2.2-rc.5`** (the current npm `latest`). The bundles are written against
the 0.2.x bundle format introduced after `0.2.0-rc.2`; they also load on `0.2.1-rc.5`.
Presets declare their plugin rows by bare package name (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash`, not
`...@0.2.2-rc.5`), so the running DSH release always supplies matching plugin versions —
nothing here needs repinning per release.

Each directory is a self-contained Cordis bundle that declares its preset as an
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row. The older layout this replaced —
`~/.dsh/.agent-presets/<id>/` holding `preset.yml` + `agent.cordis.yml` — is no longer read
by any 0.2.x release, which is why these directories carry both the new patch and the old
files for reference.

## Version requirements

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| DSH | `0.2.1-rc.5` or newer; verified on `0.2.2-rc.5` |
| Node.js | Whatever the installed DSH requires. **0.2.2+ needs Node ≥ 24.9**; earlier 0.2.x releases run on Node 22. |
| Extras | Some presets call local MCP servers or CLIs (`pdfcraft`, `gridcraft`) and expect them on the machine — see each preset's own README. |

DSH ships authoritative per-release migration notes at
`docs/upgrade-guide/` inside the installed package. Read those before upgrading across a
release line; the breaks below are only the ones that touched these presets.

## Layout

Each preset subdirectory contains:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | The bundle patch — inserts the `preset-<id>` declaration row |
| `package.json` | Bundle manifest (`dsh.bundle.patch` → `./cordis.patch.yml`) |
| `agent.cordis.yml` | Legacy entry list, kept for reference |
| `preset.yml` | Legacy display metadata (name / description / order) |
| assets | Whatever the preset carries: `skills/`, `plugin/`, `server/`, `scripts/`, `mappings/`, `reference/` |

Relative specifiers inside `cordis.patch.yml` (e.g. `name: ./plugin/mdpdf-plugin.mjs`) are
rewritten to file URLs **only** for rows inserted at the top level of an `insert:` list.
A row nested in a preset declaration's `config.plugins` is *not* rewritten: it resolves
against the profile rather than the bundle, fails to import, and the tool is silently
absent at runtime — no boot error. Those rows must use the bundle's installed package
name, `@local/dsh-preset-<id>/plugin/mdpdf-plugin.mjs`, as every preset here now does.

## Presets

| Directory | Display name |
| --- | --- |
| `chat` | Chat |
| `coding-swarm` | Coding Swarm |
| `debate-team` | Debate Team |
| `legal-financial-consul` | Legal-Financial Consul |
| `medical-technician` | Medical Technician |
| `ocr-md` | OCR to Markdown |
| `ocr-md-json` | OCR-MD-JSON |
| `property-researcher` | property-researcher |
| `researcher-browser` | Researcher |
| `research-swarm` | Research Swarm |
| `revit-tools` | Revit Tools |
| `statement-consolidator` | Statement Consolidator |
| `vacation-planner` | Vacation Planner |

Also in this repository, not a preset:

| Directory | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `vector-db/` | An Ollama `num_ctx` VRAM calculator plus the DSH knowledge-base plugin docs. No `preset.yml` / `cordis.patch.yml`, so it is not mounted as a preset — see `vector-db/README.md`. |

## Installing

Copy the preset directory wherever you keep bundles, then install by absolute path from the
DSH Web plugin page or via the plugin manager:

```
plugin_manager install_bundle /absolute/path/to/dsh-02x/<preset-id>
```

Installing executes plugin code in the Host process, so it asks for approval. After
installing, check the roster: a preset whose activation failed stays listed with a
diagnostic and cannot compose a session. Validate changed behaviour in a **new** session —
existing sessions keep the plugin revision they started with.

If you keep live copies outside the repository (this project's are under
`~/.dsh/preset-bundles/<id>/`, linked directly into the profile), copy edits back there and
reinstall the bundle.

## Upgrading DSH: why presets can look "deleted"

Worth understanding before an upgrade, because the failure is silent:

The preset registry mounts every child plugin row eagerly. If **one** row cannot be
imported, the whole mount rejects, the preset is marked `broken`, and the Web picker filters
broken rows out of the roster. A single stale specifier therefore makes a preset vanish from
the UI with no error surface — indistinguishable from data loss. Nothing is actually lost:
the bundle files are untouched, and fixing the row brings the preset back.

Two such breaks landed in the 0.2.x line, both documented in DSH's own
`docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-rc.1/subagent-control-tools/`:

- **`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents` was removed.** `list_agents` now
  registers from the parent package together with `send_message` and `interrupt_agent`.
  Delete any separate `/list-agents` row; if the plain `dsh-tool-subagent-control` row is
  already present, nothing needs replacing. Disabling that shared row now disables all
  three tools.
- **`modelSelectionSettings` was renamed to `modelSelection`** on
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent`, and model discovery became opt-in via
  `modelDiscovery: true`. Both default to false. The rename is *not* fatal — unknown config
  keys are ignored — but leaving it silently turns off child model selection.

All presets here are migrated past both. Before upgrading, you can check your own bundles the
same way: confirm every `@deepseek-ai/...` package and subpath a preset names still exists in
the target release's installed tree.

## Migration notes

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread` was retired in `0.2.0-rc.2`; the presets that
  used it now mount `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc` (same `provider: spawn` config).
- All `!!js` Loader expressions, comments and block scalars were carried over verbatim. Note
  that `!!js` is valid in bundle patches but **not** in a profile's own `cordis.patch.yml`,
  where an `!!js` entry aborts profile loading with an unknown-tag YAML error.
- `server/` directories keep `package.json` + lockfiles; `node_modules/` is not committed —
  restore with `npm ci` (or `pnpm install`) inside the server directory.
- Some presets hardcode absolute paths belonging to the original author's machine. Replace
  them with your own, or remove those rows if you do not run the backing service.
- Presets whose composition embeds a firm's private positioning, correspondence, or measured
  writing profile are not published here. Build those locally and keep their reference
  material out of any repository you share.

# Statement Consolidator

A **bookkeeper** agent preset for year-end reporting. It reads bank and
credit-card statements in **CSV or Excel** from *any* institution and *any*
layout, turns each into **canonical JSON**, learns and persists the
per-institution field mapping (**confirmed once, reused forever**), and then
consolidates many heterogeneous statement files into **ONE big file with the
same format** — a canonical JSON + CSV **"master transactions"** file plus a
**multi-sheet Excel workbook** (all transactions, account summaries,
reconciliation, continuity, duplicates, coverage gaps, exceptions, and the
mappings-used audit).

Every transformation is **model-free and deterministic**. A reconciliation gate
runs on the money (`opening + Σ transactions == closing`), duplicate and
double-import detection, cross-statement continuity, and month-coverage are
checked. **No number is ever invented and no raw column is ever silently
dropped** — unmapped headers go to `extras`, preserved verbatim.

---

## Contents

| Area | Where |
|---|---|
| What the agent does (protocol of record) | [`skills/statement-consolidation/SKILL.md`](skills/statement-consolidation/SKILL.md) |
| Canonical row / envelope (human) | [`reference/CANONICAL-SCHEMA.md`](reference/CANONICAL-SCHEMA.md) |
| Canonical row / envelope (JSON Schema) | [`reference/CANONICAL-SCHEMA.json`](reference/CANONICAL-SCHEMA.json) |
| Field-mapping profile format + confirm-once loop | [`reference/MAPPING-PROFILES.md`](reference/MAPPING-PROFILES.md) |
| Reconciliation gate (the 5 checks) | [`reference/RECONCILIATION.md`](reference/RECONCILIATION.md) |
| Built-in synonym (Tier-2) discovery table | [`reference/SYNONYMS.md`](reference/SYNONYMS.md) |
| Example mappings (start from these) | [`mappings/`](mappings/) |
| Example statements (run end-to-end from these) | [`examples/`](examples/) |
| Scripts (stdlib-only, no network) | [`scripts/`](scripts/) |

---

## What you get (the deliverable)

For a set of input statements, the preset emits (all in the workspace):

* `consolidated.json` — the big file: one canonical `rows` array under one
  schema, plus the full reconciliation / duplicates / coverage / exceptions
  audit.
* `consolidated.csv` — the same rows, flat, spreadsheet-friendly (the
  "one big spreadsheet").
* `consolidated.xlsx` — a **workbook** with one sheet per concern:

  | Sheet | What it is |
  |---|---|
  | `README` | What the file is and how it was built. |
  | `Accounts` | One row per account: totals in/out/net, fees, interest, min/max dates, dup count. |
  | `All Transactions` | Every canonical row in one fixed column layout — the "big file". |
  | `Reconciliation` | Per-statement close-check (`opening + Σ == closing`) PASS/FAIL with both numbers. |
  | `Continuity` | Per-account statement-to-statement continuity (prev closing == next opening). |
  | `Duplicates` | Rows that are re-reads or double-imports across distinct files. |
  | `Coverage Gaps` | (account, missing month) in the year scope. |
  | `Exceptions` | Accumulated anomalies (unparsed cells, unmapped → extras, dup flags, close-check fails). |
  | `Mappings Used` | Per institution-file: sign_convention, columns resolved, resolved_by, files_seen — the audit trail. |

The deliverable contract (SKILL.md §6) always ends with:
**`OUTPUTS` / `RECONCILIATION` / `ACCOUNTS` / `EXCEPTIONS` / `MAPPINGS USED`**.

---

## Install

1. **Install once** (Windows/macOS/Linux, from the preset folder):

   ```powershell
   # copy the preset into DSH's per-user preset root
   .\INSTALL.cmd
   ```

   On macOS / Linux, copy the folder into `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/`.

2. **Prerequisites**

   * **CSV path: nothing to install.** The CSV input + CSV output pipelines are
     standard-library Python (3.10+).
   * **XLSX path (reading `.xlsx` and writing the final workbook): one
     install:**

     ```powershell
     py -m pip install --user openpyxl   # Windows
     python3 -m pip install --user openpyxl   # macOS / Linux
     ```

     Without `openpyxl` you can still process CSV inputs and emit the CSV /
     JSON "master" outputs — only the `.xlsx` workbook is skipped (with a clear
     note).

3. **Pick the preset** — in the DSH GUI select **Statement Consolidator** and
   point it at the folder of CSV / XLSX statements you want to reconcile for
   the year.

---

## How it works (the 8-step pipeline)

Each file, on each run, goes through:

1. **Ingest** (`scripts/ingest.py`) — read the CSV/XLSX, auto-detect the
   header row among the institution's title / branded / summary rows, capture
   the statement envelope (period, opening / closing balance, printed total,
   summary lines), and emit a `*.raw.json` with every cell preserved. *Nothing
   is dropped*: summary lines lifted off the table are kept verbatim in
   `statement.summary_lines`.
2. **Match fields** (`scripts/apply_mapping.py`) — resolve each canonical
   field to a raw header using the institution's mapping file (Tier-1) with the
   built-in synonym table as fallback (Tier-2). Compute the *signed*
   `amount` from the institution's declared `sign_convention`; preserve
   `amount_debit` / `amount_credit`; classify fee / interest rows into typed
   subtotals; route unclaimed headers to `extras` verbatim; derive a stable
   `id`; attach provenance.
3. **Reconcile** (`scripts/consolidate.py`) — run the deterministic gate
   (close-check, continuity, duplicates, coverage) and build the deliverables.

The **confirm-once** loop (what makes "many files, many formats" cheap over
time) is described in [`reference/MAPPING-PROFILES.md`](reference/MAPPING-PROFILES.md):

```
new institution statement
    └─ header auto-detect + mapping proposal
    └─ SHOW: resolved header table + 3-row canonical sample
    └─ ask_user_question  (ONE confirmation per NEW institution)
    └─ save to <workspace>\mappings\<institution>.json
existing institution statement
    └─ apply the identical mapping (zero confirms)
```

A mapping is a small JSON file the user edits, **not** a re-rolled guess. It
lives in the workspace (`<workspace>/mappings/`), travels with the user's data,
is easy to diff in git, and is trivially deletable when an institution is
retired. This preset is generic; *your* institution memory is in the workspace.

---

## Run it yourself (no agent, just the scripts)

The shipped `examples/` + `mappings/` are intentionally tiny and reconciling
so you can see the whole pipeline in ~five lines:

```powershell
# 1. ingest
py scripts\ingest.py examples\example-bank-2025Q1.csv \
     -o work\bank.raw.json --institution "Example Bank" \
     --account-type checking --currency USD --account-masked "****4821"
py scripts\ingest.py examples\example-credit-card-2025Q1.csv \
     -o work\card.raw.json --institution "Example Card" \
     --account-type credit --currency USD --account-masked "****8890"

# 2. apply mapping  (raw -> canonical)
py scripts\apply_mapping.py work\bank.raw.json  -m mappings\example-bank.json        -o work\bank.canonical.json  --institution "Example Bank" --account-masked "****4821"
py scripts\apply_mapping.py work\card.raw.json  -m mappings\example-credit-card.json -o work\card.canonical.json --institution "Example Card" --account-masked "****8890"

# 3. consolidate + reconcile + deliverable
py scripts\consolidate.py work\bank.canonical.json work\card.canonical.json \
     -o work\consolidated.xlsx --year 2025
```

Expected summary on the shipped examples: **2/2 close-checks PASS, 0 failures,
0 duplicates, 0 coverage gaps**.

On macOS / Linux replace `py` with `python3` (or `python`).

---

## A few hard non-negotiables (see SKILL.md)

* **Money discipline.** Sums in integer cents, never float. `two-column`
  statements compute `amount = credit − debit`; `signed-amount` statements
  parse the printed signed value. Never guess — quote the two numbers.
* **Date discipline.** `date_format` is declared per-institution in the mapping.
  `3/4/2025` is March 4 *in that institution's mapping* — that decision is
  auditable, not a guess.
* **No data loss.** `extras` holds every unmapped raw header verbatim; `raw`
  holds the full original row; `summary_lines` holds the lifted statement
  lines. `ignore[]` is the only way a header leaves the audit.
* **Stable IDs.** Row identity is `sha1-16` over (institution, account, date,
  description, amount, reference). Re-reads and double-imports are detected by
  this ID + an independent content signature.
* **The deliverable always ends** with `OUTPUTS` / `RECONCILIATION` /
  `ACCOUNTS` / `EXCEPTIONS` / `MAPPINGS USED`.

---

## What this preset is NOT

* **Not a PDF extractor.** PDF statements are out of scope on purpose — the
  companion [`ocr-md`](https://github.com/search?q=ocr-md) / `ocr-md-json`
  presets convert PDF → structured Markdown / JSON before this preset sees
  them. Pipe: `pdf → ocr-md → csv/xlsx → this preset`.
* **Not a tax / accounting engine.** It reconciles statements and produces a
  "big file" for your accountant or your own bookkeeping. It does not post
  entries, compute tax, or produce financial statements.
* **Not a cloud service.** No network, no API keys, no PHI beyond what the
  user already put in the input files (account numbers arrive pre-masked).

---

## Layout

```
statement-consolidator/
├─ agent.cordis.yml            # DSH persona: Bookkeeper / statement-consolidator
├─ preset.yml                  # display name + description
├─ INSTALL.cmd                 # one-shot deploy + prerequisite report (no auto-install)
├─ LICENSE                     # MIT
├─ README.md                   # this file
├─ skills/
│   └─ statement-consolidation/
│       └─ SKILL.md            # the protocol of record (8 steps, discipline, deliverable contract)
├─ reference/
│   ├─ CANONICAL-SCHEMA.md     # human-readable schema
│   ├─ CANONICAL-SCHEMA.json   # JSON Schema (draft-07) — validate your canonical files
│   ├─ MAPPING-PROFILES.md     # mapping file reference + confirm-once loop
│   ├─ RECONCILIATION.md       # the 5 checks + the gate's report shape
│   └─ SYNONYMS.md             # built-in Tier-2 discovery table
├─ mappings/
│   ├─ README.md
│   ├─ example-bank.json       # generic (no real institution) — start from this
│   └─ example-credit-card.json
├─ examples/
│   ├─ example-bank-2025Q1.csv        # two-column, checking (reconciles)
│   └─ example-credit-card-2025Q1.csv # signed-amount, credit  (reconciles)
└─ scripts/
    ├─ lib/
    │   ├─ __init__.py
    │   └─ common.py           # stdlib helpers: money, dates, stable_id, norm_header, SYNONYMS
    ├─ ingest.py               # CSV/XLSX -> raw statement JSON (header auto-detect)
    ├─ apply_mapping.py        # raw -> canonical rows (Tier-1 mapping, Tier-2 synonyms)
    └─ consolidate.py          # merge + reconcile + emit JSON/CSV/XLSX workbook
```

---

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# Vacation Planner — a DSH agent preset for gourmet travel planning

A [DeepSeek Harness](http://127.0.0.1) **agent preset** that turns a session into a
**food-first travel planner** for serious foodies: people who book trips around
tasting menus and new openings, care about museums, markets, and what is actually
on in town, and are equally happy at a two-star counter or a well-sited campsite.
It researches where to stay, eat, drink, and visit; aligns the plan with local
events; works out the flights, trains, and transfers; and delivers a day-by-day
itinerary file with a booking checklist — notes to act on, not narrative prose.

## What's in here

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `agent.cordis.yml` | The preset composition — the full shipped `standard` toolset (shell, filesystem, web search + fetch, skills, goals, plan mode, compaction, delegation + workflow, jobs) with the persona swapped to a **gourmet travel planner**, plan mode re-aimed at itinerary planning, and a clock context row for reservation-window math. |
| `preset.yml` | Metadata (name / description) shown by the roster & settings UI. |
| `skills/gourmet-travel-method/SKILL.md` | The bundled method skill — the planner's operating manual (below). Bundling it under `skills/` is what makes it auto-discoverable for this preset. |
| `LICENSE` | MIT. |

## How it plans

The `gourmet-travel-method` skill carries the method. The highlights:

**Taste-source hierarchy.** Editorial sources judge taste; crowd aggregates never
do. Promoted: **Eater** (Eater 38 / Heatmap for "new and hot"), **Michelin**
(Stars, Bib Gourmand, Keys), local critics and city media, World's 50 Best /
La Liste as of-the-moment radar, NYT / Bon Appétit / Food & Wine. **Demoted to
logistics-only:** Yelp, TripAdvisor, and Google review scores — hours, phones,
complaint scans; never rankings. Every taste claim names its source.

**Reservation mechanics.** A per-city platform map (Resy Notify, Tock's ~9–10 a.m.
cancellation window, SevenRooms, OpenTable, Japan's Pocket Concierge / OMAKASE /
TableCheck), drop-time skepticism (never plan around a forum-posted drop time —
confirm by phone), the escalation ladder (alert → weekday-morning call → concierge
→ card dining programs → paid secondary), and the value moves (bar/counter seats,
lunch at the same kitchen, Bib Gourmand filling).

**Events first.** Tourism-board calendars, Time Out, museum exhibition pages with
timed-entry booking, festival and market-day calendars, closure days — all on one
timeline **before** any dinner is fixed, because events dictate which neighborhood
the traveler occupies at which hour.

**Transit that respects the table.** Google Flights / ITA Matrix / Skyscanner for
air; The Man in Seat 61's booking horizons for rail (Eurostar ~11 months,
SNCF/Trenitalia ~4, DB up to 12/6, Renfe erratic); airport transfer buffers; and
the hard rule: **no fixed reservation on arrival day without a 3-hour buffer.**

**Luxury to camping.** "Stay where you eat" for hotels (Michelin Keys, Mr & Mrs
Smith, Design Hotels), Hipcamp / Pitchup / Canopy & Stars for the outdoors end —
with camping legs placed on relaxed market-and-picnic days near the dinner anchor,
never 45 minutes from a late reservation.

**Pacing and craft.** One anchor per half-day, district clustering, regional
meal-time customs, jet-lag day 1 kept reservation-free, a same-neighborhood
fallback for every anchor, one splurge per day balanced by markets and counters,
and a tourist-trap filter (menu photos, touts, prime-square locations).

**Verify and deliver.** Every fact checked against the official source and
date-stamped (`checked 2025-06-14 via museum site`); unconfirmed items flagged
`[VERIFY]`. The deliverable is `itinerary-<slug>-<start-date>.md`: trip frame,
day-by-day table, deadline-ordered booking checklist (platform, drop date,
confirmation #, cancellation deadline), budget mix, verification log, and open
questions — plus a custom Google Maps list of the anchors on request.

## What the agent will not do

It plans; it does not purchase. Bookings, payments, and venue contact happen on
the traveler's side (or by explicit instruction in a normal, non-plan session) —
plan mode explicitly forbids booking, reserving, purchasing, or writing trip
files until the plan is approved.

## Install

> **Zero-setup path — let DSH install it for you.** In any DSH session, just
> point it at this repository:
>
> > "Install the agent preset at
> > https://github.com/Axotopia/dsh/tree/main/vacation-planner, and verify it
> > mounts — start a session on the Vacation Planner mode. Grant Full Access to
> > the filesystem for this job."
>
> Full Access is needed only because the preset lands *outside* the session
> workspace (`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\.agent-presets\`). There are no dependencies
> to install: the preset is YAML + one skill, and all model traffic goes through
> your existing DSH provider configuration.

Manual path — copy this folder into any preset root DSH scans:

- **Windows:** `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\.agent-presets\vacation-planner`
- **macOS / Linux:** `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/vacation-planner`

```powershell
Copy-Item .\vacation-planner $env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\.agent-presets\vacation-planner -Recurse
```

Then pick **Vacation Planner** as the session mode in DSH.

## Use

1. Select the **Vacation Planner** preset as your session mode.
2. Frame the trip — dates, party, budget shape, dietary restrictions, splurge
   appetite, lodging style (design hotel ↔ camping). It asks only what you own
   and researches the rest.
3. Ask for the trip — e.g. *"Plan 5 days in San Sebastián in October for two:
   one splurge dinner per day, gluten-free, one night glamping in the hills"* —
   and get a day-by-day itinerary file with the booking checklist, plus map
   links. Multi-city trips fan venue/event/transit research out to subagents.

## Design notes

- **Derived from `standard`**: the tool rows are the full coding-agent toolset
  unchanged — research, not coding, is this agent's workload, and the same rows
  serve it (web tools are the maps, guides, calendars, and booking engines;
  the filesystem holds itinerary files; delegation fans research out).
- **`time-context` enabled** (15-minute refresh): a durable clock reading so
  drop dates, event calendars, and "what's open this week" anchor to today.
- **Plan mode re-aimed**: the shipped plan-mode contract's mechanics are kept
  (explore before executing, `exit_plan_mode` presentation) with the exploration
  defined as web research and execution defined as booking/writing files.
- **Realm discipline preserved** from `standard`: per-agent state (plan mode,
  compaction) stays behind entry-local isolate realms; rows that publish
  nothing sit loose, exactly as the shipped composition documents.

## Disclaimer

These presets are proof-of-concept models, not drop-in production solutions.
Review the composition (`agent.cordis.yml`), persona, and skill, and adapt them
to your use cases. Itineraries are research assistance, not reservations:
venues, events, hours, and fares change — the verification log tells you what
was checked and when, and everything flagged `[VERIFY]` needs a human check
before you rely on it.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# dsh-02x

Custom agent presets for **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x**, one installable bundle per subdirectory.

**Tested on DSH `0.2.2-rc.5`** (the current npm `latest`). The bundles are written against
the 0.2.x bundle format introduced after `0.2.0-rc.2`; they also load on `0.2.1-rc.5`.
Presets declare their plugin rows by bare package name (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash`, not
`...@0.2.2-rc.5`), so the running DSH release always supplies matching plugin versions —
nothing here needs repinning per release.

Each directory is a self-contained Cordis bundle that declares its preset as an
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row. The older layout this replaced —
`~/.dsh/.agent-presets/<id>/` holding `preset.yml` + `agent.cordis.yml` — is no longer read
by any 0.2.x release, which is why these directories carry both the new patch and the old
files for reference.

## Version requirements

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| DSH | `0.2.1-rc.5` or newer; verified on `0.2.2-rc.5` |
| Node.js | Whatever the installed DSH requires. **0.2.2+ needs Node ≥ 24.9**; earlier 0.2.x releases run on Node 22. |
| Extras | Some presets call local MCP servers or CLIs (`pdfcraft`, `gridcraft`) and expect them on the machine — see each preset's own README. |

DSH ships authoritative per-release migration notes at
`docs/upgrade-guide/` inside the installed package. Read those before upgrading across a
release line; the breaks below are only the ones that touched these presets.

## Layout

Each preset subdirectory contains:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | The bundle patch — inserts the `preset-<id>` declaration row |
| `package.json` | Bundle manifest (`dsh.bundle.patch` → `./cordis.patch.yml`) |
| `agent.cordis.yml` | Legacy entry list, kept for reference |
| `preset.yml` | Legacy display metadata (name / description / order) |
| assets | Whatever the preset carries: `skills/`, `plugin/`, `server/`, `scripts/`, `mappings/`, `reference/` |

Relative specifiers inside `cordis.patch.yml` (e.g. `name: ./plugin/mdpdf-plugin.mjs`) are
rewritten to file URLs **only** for rows inserted at the top level of an `insert:` list.
A row nested in a preset declaration's `config.plugins` is *not* rewritten: it resolves
against the profile rather than the bundle, fails to import, and the tool is silently
absent at runtime — no boot error. Those rows must use the bundle's installed package
name, `@local/dsh-preset-<id>/plugin/mdpdf-plugin.mjs`, as every preset here now does.

## Presets

| Directory | Display name |
| --- | --- |
| `chat` | Chat |
| `coding-swarm` | Coding Swarm |
| `debate-team` | Debate Team |
| `legal-financial-consul` | Legal-Financial Consul |
| `medical-technician` | Medical Technician |
| `ocr-md` | OCR to Markdown |
| `ocr-md-json` | OCR-MD-JSON |
| `property-researcher` | property-researcher |
| `researcher-browser` | Researcher |
| `research-swarm` | Research Swarm |
| `revit-tools` | Revit Tools |
| `statement-consolidator` | Statement Consolidator |
| `vacation-planner` | Vacation Planner |

Also in this repository, not a preset:

| Directory | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `vector-db/` | An Ollama `num_ctx` VRAM calculator plus the DSH knowledge-base plugin docs. No `preset.yml` / `cordis.patch.yml`, so it is not mounted as a preset — see `vector-db/README.md`. |

## Installing

Copy the preset directory wherever you keep bundles, then install by absolute path from the
DSH Web plugin page or via the plugin manager:

```
plugin_manager install_bundle /absolute/path/to/dsh-02x/<preset-id>
```

Installing executes plugin code in the Host process, so it asks for approval. After
installing, check the roster: a preset whose activation failed stays listed with a
diagnostic and cannot compose a session. Validate changed behaviour in a **new** session —
existing sessions keep the plugin revision they started with.

If you keep live copies outside the repository (this project's are under
`~/.dsh/preset-bundles/<id>/`, linked directly into the profile), copy edits back there and
reinstall the bundle.

## Upgrading DSH: why presets can look "deleted"

Worth understanding before an upgrade, because the failure is silent:

The preset registry mounts every child plugin row eagerly. If **one** row cannot be
imported, the whole mount rejects, the preset is marked `broken`, and the Web picker filters
broken rows out of the roster. A single stale specifier therefore makes a preset vanish from
the UI with no error surface — indistinguishable from data loss. Nothing is actually lost:
the bundle files are untouched, and fixing the row brings the preset back.

Two such breaks landed in the 0.2.x line, both documented in DSH's own

- **`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents` was removed.** `list_agents` now
  registers from the parent package together with `send_message` and `interrupt_agent`.
  Delete any separate `/list-agents` row; if the plain `dsh-tool-subagent-control` row is
  already present, nothing needs replacing. Disabling that shared row now disables all
  three tools.

# 澄境 | Limina

**阅人际，留寸心。** *Glean the World, Guard the Heart.*

装在 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端的阅读器：订阅你信得过的作者，读原文或中文版本，
把电子书读下去、听下去，然后把当前这一页丢给 Harness 里的模型接着问。

零第三方后端 —— 订阅自包含，书架只读**你自己配的源**（本机目录或你自己的网盘）。

`MIT` · 25 个 agent 工具 · 全部数据在本机

---

## 能做什么

| 模块 | 说明 | 细节 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **订阅** | RSS 2.0 / Atom / RDF，最多 100 个源；分组、补全历史、停更标记 | [订阅与信息源](docs/features.md#订阅与信息源) |
| **阅读** | 正文净化、六种纸色、字号 / 行高 / 版心可调、大纲、⌘F 搜索 | [阅读体验](docs/features.md#阅读体验) |
| **翻译** | 原文 / 双语 / 中文三态；字幕走 Google 优先，剩下的交给模型 | [翻译与对照](docs/features.md#翻译与对照) |
| **听** | 播客单集边听边跟字幕；电子书朗读；没字幕可**本机识别**（音频不出本机） | [播客、字幕与语音](docs/features.md#播客字幕与语音) |
| **电子书** | PDF 按原版式；EPUB / MOBI / AZW3 / AZW / TXT 重排；目录、书内搜索、划线笔记 | [电子书](docs/features.md#电子书) |
| **解读与导出** | 抽正文 → 切章 → 逐章中文解读；整本导出成 agent 可按需加载的 skill 包 | [电子书](docs/features.md#电子书) |
| **日记** | 第三个 tab，一天一篇；灵感速记 `L`；私密条目独立加密、不进模型 | [日记与灵感](docs/features.md#日记与灵感) |
| **论文** | 第四个 tab：导入、摘要、找相关、页级翻译、引用 | [论文](docs/features.md#论文) |
| **给 agent 用** | 25 个工具：`rss_*` / `book_*` / `diary_*` / `paper_*` | [Agent 能力](docs/agent-tools.md) |

## 安装

插件装进 **DeepSeek Harness 桌面端**。`desktop` profile 由 Electron App 独占管理，
命令行 `dsh plugin --profile desktop …` 一律被拒 —— **用 GUI 装**。

1. 把仓库 clone 到本机任意目录，记下它的绝对路径；
2. 侧栏点 **「插件」**；
3. **「添加插件」** → 粘贴那个绝对路径 → **「立即启用」**；
4. **完全退出 App（`Cmd+Q`）再打开**，回到面板强刷 `Cmd+Shift+R`。

第 4 步不能省：插件在 Host 半区注册服务与本机 HTTP 路由，不重启不生效。
装好后日志出现 `dsh-npie-reader: service started`，侧栏出现「阅读器」入口。

细节（`link:` 前缀、对账机制、`failed to import` 排查）见
[安装与启动细节](docs/development.md#安装与启动细节)。

## 开发

```bash
npm install
npm run build     # lib/ 不入库，发布前现建
npm test          # 单元测试
npm run verify    # 构建 + 单测 + 契约守卫
```

带真 Chrome 的视觉 / 布局检查需要本机浏览器，单独跑 `npm run verify:all`。
完整命令、守卫脚本与内部契约见 [开发](docs/development.md)。

## 已知边界

- **不抓公众号**：做不到，只能读你自己搭的转 RSS 服务。
- **电子书不还原图片与原版式**（EPUB / MOBI / AZW3），要原版式请先转 PDF。
- **云端语音识别会上传音频**，界面上明说；本机识别则不出本机。
- **翻译与解读只用 Harness 当前选中的模型**，插件不代付、不代理。

做不到的、故意不做的、已知没解决的，全部列在 [边界与已知限制](docs/limits.md)。

## 文档

| 文档 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| [功能详解](docs/features.md) | 48 项功能的完整说明，以及每一项「为什么这么做」 |
| [Agent 能力](docs/agent-tools.md) | 工具语义、时间窗、检索闸门、内置目录取舍 |
| [设计笔记](docs/design-notes.md) | 已修正的缺陷：现象 / 根因 / 修法 / 守卫用例 |
| [开发](docs/development.md) | 构建、测试、守卫脚本、契约、数据位置、安装细节 |
| [边界与限制](docs/limits.md) | 做不到的、故意不做的、已知没解决的 |
| [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) | 逐版本变更 |

## 许可

MIT（`Copyright (c) 2026 Banny`）。第三方组件的许可与版权行见
[THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md)：pdf.js（Apache-2.0）、
Milkdown（MIT）、agentero motif（MIT）、chinese-independent-blogs（MIT）、shuting（MIT）。

The patch resolves to lib/index.js and lib/client.js, absent from the fixed archive, while src/host/index.js and its source modules are present. The prepack build was not run and a corresponding distributable was not mapped. Capabilities include file/ebook parsing, remote feeds, speech and private diary data. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-wishcoder-devteam

> 一个 DSH bundle、**一个**预设：`devteam`（DevTeam-20 · 资深融合开发团队），内置「许愿：」模式。
> 装一次，改代码和「从零做一个东西」走同一个入口，不用在新建会话时二选一。

- 版本：`0.0.101`
- 类型：DSH agent preset bundle（`dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`）
- 许可：MIT
- 仓库：`github.com/bingyi0321/dsh-wishcoder-devteam`

---

## 1. 这是什么

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）的预设（preset）决定一个会话的 persona、挂哪些工具、怎么压缩上下文、能加载哪些技能。本包只提供一个预设：

| preset id | 显示名 | order | 取向 | 技能 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `devteam`（`cordis.patch.yml` 里的行 id 是 `preset-devteam`） | DevTeam-20 · 资深融合开发团队 | 20 | 改现有代码走最短路径（最小 diff、最少 token、最快出结果）；许愿式任务走「许愿：」模式 | 8 个，见 §5 |

同一份 persona 里用一行路由把两种跑法分开：

- **日常改代码**（默认）：`grep -n` 定位唯一最小改动点 → 改 → 跑一条自测 → 报「改了哪个文件 + 一行理由」。
- **许愿**（用户以「许愿：」开头，或要整页/整功能/从零做）：加载 `wish-loop`，走「不提问 → 先写会失败的验收 → 全绿才交付 → 三行收尾（改动/验证/残留）」；此时 persona 里「>3 文件先问是否扩大范围」**不适用**。

本包的前身是两个并列预设（`devteam` + `wishcoder`，v0.0.1）。第二个入口在发布后 6.5 小时的 385 个会话里被选了 **0 次**，且两段 persona 在同一触发条件下要求相反动作，因此 v0.0.101 起折叠成一个入口——**只合入口，不合 persona**。

## 2. 为什么是单入口

1. **没被选用**：全量扫 385 个会话头的 `agentPreset` → devteam 246（63.9%）/ standard 92 / optimizer 29 / cordis 10 / miniprogram 6 / (none) 2 / **wishcoder 0**。
2. **不能真合并**：两套规则在「>3 文件或 >50 行」上动作相反（`先问「是否确认扩大改动范围？」` vs `先落 SPEC 再动，不提问`）。硬塞进一段会重演已知的自相矛盾缺陷。
3. **合并省不到 token**：未选中的预设不组装、不进请求，两个定义并存对每请求成本为 0。真实成本只有「建会话时二选一、选错只能重开」——预设是**会话级绑定**，中途换不了。
4. 所以只把**选择面**收成一个：许愿能力由 `wish-loop` / `verify-harness` 两个技能承载（技能正文不进前缀缓存，随改随生效），触发词写在 persona，规则细节留在技能里。

取证与三段对比：`D:\agent\.research\preset-merge-decision-2026-11-20.md`。

## 3. 安装

### 3.1 放进 profile 的 bundle 列表

在 DSH profile（例如 `C:\Users\Administrator\.dsh\profiles\desktop`）的 `package.json` 里两处各加一行：

```jsonc
{
  "dependencies": { "dsh-wishcoder-devteam": "link:D:\\agent\\dsh-wishcoder-devteam" },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["dsh-wishcoder-devteam"] } }
}
```

改完**重启 DSH**。"什么算生效"的标准是：新建会话的会话头里 `agentPreset` 是 `devteam`。

### 3.2 确认技能目录

`cordis.patch.yml` 里 `customSkillDirs` 是绝对路径，默认指向本机安装位置：

```yaml
customSkillDirs:
  - 'D:\agent\dsh-wishcoder-devteam\skills'
```

换机器/换目录只改这一处，然后跑门禁（§7）：

```
node D:\agent\dsh-wishcoder-devteam\validate.cjs
```

### 3.3 选预设

- **单个会话**：新建会话 → 预设选择器选「DevTeam-20 · 资深融合开发团队」。
- **设为默认**：设置 → 通用 → 默认预设；或 profile 层 `agent-preset-registry.default` / `selectedDefault`。
  注意 `agent-preset-registry.config` 是整段替换、不是深合并——改 `selectedDefault` 时要把 `default` 一起保留。

### 3.4 卸载

profile `package.json` 删掉那两行 → 重启。预设与技能随 bundle 一起消失，不写别的目录。

## 4. 怎么用

### 4.1 日常改代码（默认模式）

```
把这个接口的分页参数从 page 改成 cursor，别动其他调用点。
```

预期动作：定位唯一最小改动点 → 改 → 一条自测 → 一句「改了哪个文件 + 为什么」。

```
重构支付模块，把三个回调合成一个状态机。
```

跨文件的活走 `devteam-flow`：需求澄清 → 契约拆分 → 并行实现 → 评审放行；写域不重叠的块用子代理扇出。

### 4.2 许愿（加前缀）

```
许愿：做个能把手机截图批量裁成 1080x1920 并加圆角的小工具，双击能跑。
```

预期动作：写 SPEC → 写 `scripts/verify.ps1` → 跑红 → 实现 → 跑绿 → 报三行（改动 / 验证 / 残留）。
不满意就补一句（「圆角要 24px」），它把这条加进验收再跑一遍——**验收是唯一的口径**，不靠自我感觉。

### 4.3 带约束许愿（最省返工）

```
许愿：<一句话说清要做什么>
验收：<怎么算做对了，能给命令最好>
不许动：<目录 / 接口 / 依赖>
预算：<几轮内、别超多少改动>
```

### 4.4 触发词

| 说法 | 进哪个模式 |
| --- | --- |
| 「改一下 / 修一下 / 加个字段 / 怎么报错了」 | 日常改（最小 diff） |
| 「许愿：…」 | 许愿（`wish-loop`） |
| 「做个…/从零/整页/整功能/端到端」 | 许愿（persona 路由行；拿不准就自己加「许愿：」，最省事） |
| 「这个文件重构一下」 | `devteam-flow`（跨文件编排） |

## 5. 技能（8 个）

`skills/` 下 8 个目录，一次性全部可发现（`includeDefaultRoots: false`，只有本包的技能）：

| 技能 | 什么时候用 |
| --- | --- |
| `devteam-flow` | 多文件改动、重构、需求→契约→并行实现→评审 |
| `web-platform` | 前端/Node 服务：路由、状态、构建、接口联调 |
| `android-app` | 改安卓工程、构建、真机验证（adb/logcat/uidump） |
| `embedded-firmware` | 固件、串口、板级调试 |
| `debug-research` | 现象→假设→最小复现的排障，别盲调 |
| `win-desktop` | Windows 桌面程序、注册表、服务、打包 |
| `wish-loop` | 许愿闭环：验收先行、三振换法、交付前三行 |
| `verify-harness` | 写可执行的验收脚本（`scripts/verify.ps1`），全绿判定 |

前 6 个是**开发角色**（进 `roles.json` 注册表，新增须批准登记）；`wish-loop` / `verify-harness` 是**许愿闭环**，走 `validate.cjs` 的 `NON_ROLE_SKILLS` 白名单，不占角色名额。

## 6. 预设置里挂了什么（18 行）

| # | 行 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `persona` | 1000 字符的团队意志（输出/范围/许愿/验收/底线/步数/改动/验证/环境/记忆/成本/技能） |
| 2 | `agent-instructions` | 注入工作区 `AGENTS.md`（限字节，避免把大文件塞进前缀） |
| 3 | `time-context` | 当前时间 |
| 4–5 | `tool-bash` / `tool-pwsh` | shell；本机只有 `powershell.exe` 5.1，没有 `pwsh` |
| 6–7 | `tool-fs` / `tool-fs-search` | 读写与 `grep`/`glob`（限额收紧，防止一次 `--full` 灌爆上下文） |
| 8 | `repeat-tool-reminder` | 同一调用重复时提醒换参数 |
| 9 | `tool-jobs` | 后台任务 |
| 10 | `skill-filesystem` | 技能根：本包 `skills/`，`watch: false`（技能改动不冲前缀缓存） |
| 11 | `tool-skill` | 加载技能正文 |
| 12–14 | `planning` / `compaction` / `delegation` | 计划、压缩、子代理（含深度上限） |
| 15 | `tool-ask-user` | 问用户 |
| 16 | `tool-todo` | 待办板 |
| 17 | `tool-web` | **`disabled: true`**（无 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` 时联网必失败；要用先配 key 再删那行 disabled） |
| 18 | `present` | 交付文件（图片/Office/文档卡片） |

**不声明** `permission` / `permissionPresets`：那是内核级服务，preset 作用域再挂一次会让预设组装失败、新会话直接建不出来（历史事故，见 `cordis.patch.yml` 文件头注释）。

## 7. 自检门禁

```
node D:\agent\dsh-wishcoder-devteam\validate.cjs
```

覆盖：

1. `package.json` 可解析、版本与 bundle 声明一致；
2. 顶层**只有一个** `- insert:`、**恰好一个** preset 行、单 preset 18 插件行、order 无碰撞；
3. 无内核级服务行（`permission` / `permissionPresets`）；
4. persona 500~1000 字符且含「最小 diff / 底线 / 许愿： / wish-loop」；
5. `customSkillDirs` 指向本包、每个技能有 `SKILL.md` 且 front-matter `name` 与目录名一致；
6. `roles.json` 与 `skills/` 双向登记（`active` 角色全在、技能不 stray、许愿技能走白名单）；
7. 文本卫生：无 U+FFFD、无零宽字符、无 BOM。

退出 `0` = 通过，`1` = 失败（逐条打到 stderr）。**改完任何文件都要跑。**

## 8. 目录

```
dsh-wishcoder-devteam/
├─ package.json      # name/version + dsh.bundle.patch
├─ cordis.patch.yml  # 唯一入口：一个 - insert:，一个 preset 行（devteam order 20）
├─ validate.cjs      # 门禁
├─ roles.json        # 开发角色注册表（6 个 active，maxSkills 6）
├─ skills/           # 8 个技能
├─ CHANGELOG.md
├─ LICENSE
└─ README.md
```

`cordis.patch.yml` 保留了源文件的全部历史注释（v4→v22 的改动理由与实测数据）。**出问题先读那里**，比读本文档快。

## 9. 版本与发布

- 版本号走 `0.0.x`（tag `v0.0.101`），与仓库 tag 一一对应。
- 发版三步：改 `package.json` / `validate.cjs` 里的版本 → `CHANGELOG.md` 记「为什么 / 改动 / 已知取舍」 → 跑门禁 → `git tag v0.0.x` 并推送。
- 宿主装载以**重启**为准：bundle 列表与预设定义在进程启动时读，改完不重启，新建会话仍用旧定义。

当前版本 `0.0.101` 的变更见 [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)。

## 10. 已知限制与排障

| 现象 | 原因 | 处理 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 新建会话失败 / 预设列表里没有 DevTeam | 预设组装报错（多为内核级服务行重复、或 YAML 语法） | 看 `C:\Users\Administrator\.dsh\logs\desktop-next.log` 尾部的 `host.kernel.*` 报错；跑 validate |
| 技能不出现 | `customSkillDirs` 是绝对路径且指错机器 | 改 §3.2 那一处，重跑 validate，重启 |
| 许愿模式没被触发 | 没加「许愿：」，或任务描述不含"整页/整功能/从零" | 自己加前缀，最稳 |
| 宿主的 `office` / `hyperframes` 技能不见了 | `includeDefaultRoots: false`（沿用 devteam，省约 1.2k 字符/请求） | 要文档/视频能力就把该行改 `true` 并跑 validate |
| persona 改不动了 | 已顶 1000 字符上限 | 先删一条旧规则再加（护栏，不是 bug） |
| 联网工具报错 | `tool-web` 默认 disabled | 配 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` 后删 `disabled: true` 那行 |
| 老会话报 preset 不存在 | 该会话记录的 `agentPreset` 是已删的 `wishcoder` | 新建会话；实测这类会话数为 0 |

## 11. 许可

MIT，见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-plugin-chrome-controller

Use a Chrome extension to give DeepSeek Harness browser tools for the Chrome window you are already using. The extension pairs with a local DSH Web instance and controls tabs through Chrome's debugger API.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness Web on the same computer as Chrome.
- Chrome 116 or later.
- DSH Web bound to `127.0.0.1` at a local URL such as `http://127.0.0.1:3080`. Open it once to copy the pairing code during setup.

The plugin refuses to start if DSH Web is not bound to `127.0.0.1`. The first version supports DSH Web. Headless and CLI profiles do not provide the authenticated browser pairing route. The default Web profile includes the credential store; custom compositions must provide one. The linked package has no extra runtime package dependencies to install.

## Install the DSH plugin

From a terminal with DSH installed:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web install "link:C:/path/to/dsh-plugin-chrome-controller"
```

Restart DSH Web and reload its page after installation or an update.

## Load the Chrome extension

1. Open `chrome://extensions`.
2. Turn on Developer mode.
3. Select **Load unpacked** and choose this package's `extension` folder. Approve HTTP and HTTPS site access when Chrome asks.
4. Open DSH Web yourself in an authenticated browser. Choose **Settings**, then **Chrome browser**, and copy the pairing code. The direct page is `http://127.0.0.1:3080/api/dsh-browser-extension/pairing` (use your DSH Web origin if the port differs).
5. Open the extension popup, choose **Settings**, enter the DSH Web origin and pairing code, and save.
6. Click **Connect to DSH Web** in the popup. Connecting does not open a DSH tab.

DSH stores the pairing code in its credential store. The Chrome browser section in DSH Settings shows and rotates it. The extension saves it in Chrome's local extension storage, which is restricted to trusted extension contexts but is not encrypted on disk. The service worker exchanges the code for a short-lived, single-use token, then a browser session token kept in Chrome's session storage. Tokens travel in JSON bodies, not URLs, and neither side writes them to logs. With **Connect automatically** enabled, the extension connects on Chrome start and retries after interruptions without opening a tab. Rotating the code disconnects the extension; save the new code in extension Settings before reconnecting. **Disconnect** stops current retries. Disable automatic connection in Settings to keep it disconnected on the next Chrome start.

The extension requests access to HTTP and HTTPS websites so it can inject the virtual cursor overlay on tabs you ask it to control. Chrome warns that the debugger permission can control browser tabs and that the downloads permission can manage downloads. The overlay is cosmetic; page input is sent through Chrome's debugger API.

Open the extension popup and select **Settings** to customize typing delays and key holds, longer pauses, cursor speed and arc, drag duration, and the delay between sequence steps. Each setting has a description and allowed range. The defaults are the project's tested baseline. Changing them may cause sites to flag or restrict activity; no settings guarantee a site will accept interactions.

The extension Settings page has a **DSH Web connection** section for the local origin, saved pairing code, and automatic connection toggle. The code field stays blank after saving; leave it blank to keep the saved code, or paste a new code after rotation. The page shows the DSH pairing page address for the current origin. The popup's **Connect** button uses these saved settings without opening a DSH tab.

Once paired, the extension keeps its Manifest V3 service worker alive on its own: a 30-second heartbeat alarm wakes the worker if Chrome suspends it, and a 25-second `chrome.runtime.getPlatformInfo()` call resets the worker's idle timer while it runs. Browser tools therefore respond without opening the extension popup. After updating the extension, reload it on `chrome://extensions` and click **Connect** again. The saved pairing code remains in extension Settings; copy a new one if it was rotated. Reload any page that had an element watcher running before the update.

## Element notes

1. Open the extension popup and click **Note Mode**, or right-click an element and choose **DSH Note Mode**. When the right-click target is available, the picker highlights it and shows **Add note**. Otherwise, select an element with the picker.
2. Point at an element. Press Up to select a larger container or Down to narrow the selection, then click to use the highlighted area. Use the position menu to move the controls to any corner of the viewport.
3. Write your note and click **Save note**. Note Mode resumes so you can select another element. Click **Done** or press Escape when you're finished.
4. In DSH, ask "Read my notes for this site" to find notes from any page on the same hostname and port, or ask for notes on this exact page.

**Page Notes** lists notes from the current site and shows numbered outlines for notes on the exact page you are viewing. Use **Locate** to scroll to a marked element, or follow the page link for a note saved on another page. **All Notes** shows the source URL on each note and lets you filter, edit, and delete notes across sites. Ask DSH to "Read my master list of notes" to see that list in chat. In either list, click **Delete** twice within 200 milliseconds to remove a note.

Older notes are listed under **Unknown page** until you open the original page in Note Mode or Page Notes, or ask DSH to read notes from that exact page. You can edit or delete those notes from All Notes at any time. All Notes shows the original address when Chrome has recorded it. Page Notes and the DSH tool show source addresses without query strings or fragments.

The picker works on HTML pages and can select an iframe or shadow host as a whole. If the page layout changes, check that the XPath still identifies the intended element.

## Browser tools

- `dsh_browser_tabs` lists tabs or opens, activates, and closes one.
- `dsh_browser_frames` lists every frame of a tab, including cross-origin app frames, with its integer `frameId`, URL, origin, and title. Pass that `frameId` to frame-aware snapshot, HTML, evaluation, element-watch, or workbook tools. Frame IDs change on navigation.
- `dsh_browser_element_watch` records observed changes to one element's value while you navigate (e.g. click through spreadsheet cells). A single `read` returns the log; inspect it for missing or stale entries. `action` is `start`, `stop`, or `read` (default); pass `selector` plus optional `labelSelector`, or `preset: "excel-online"` to watch the Excel formula bar labelled by the name box. Entries are capped at 5000, values at 500 chars; `clear: true` clears the log after reading while the watcher continues.
- `dsh_browser_workbook_values` attempts to read the active Excel Online sheet's used range from its app frame in one call. Pass the Excel frame's `frameId` from `dsh_browser_frames`. It checks EWA namespaces, the WAC cross-frame control, `grid.usedRange`, `grid.mc.sheets`, and direct grid object members for compatible range methods. On success it returns a value matrix, a populated map, the range address, and the method used. Reads are limited to 10,000 cells and 1,000,000 result characters. Live Excel support is still being verified; the element watcher is the reliable fallback.
- `dsh_browser_workbook_probe` reports Excel API globals and selected WAC internals in the app frame. It includes the full grid controller prototype, one level of its object members, and the shapes of `grid.usedRange`, `grid.mc.sheets`, and sheet model entries under `grid.nGi`. It does not return property values, cell contents, or access tokens. Use it when `dsh_browser_workbook_values` reports that no compatible API is available.
- `dsh_browser_workbook_file` tries Excel's used-range text endpoint when available and then the WOPI file endpoint from an Office Online app frame. It returns either text or base64 file bytes. Excel Online may reject both requests, so prefer `dsh_browser_workbook_values` or the element watcher. The access token stays inside the extension process.
- `dsh_browser_navigate` opens an HTTP or HTTPS URL in a tab and waits for loading to finish before returning the final URL.
- `dsh_browser_back`, `dsh_browser_forward`, and `dsh_browser_reload` operate on tab history and wait for the resulting load. Back and forward report whether navigation was observed.
- `dsh_browser_wait_for_change` waits for a unique element's text, form value, or attribute to change. Use `action: "arm"` before triggering an update, then wait with the returned `watchId` to catch changes that already happened. Each watch retains the last 30 changes. The watch expires after 10 minutes without a wait call, and the default wait is 10 minutes or the harness timeout if it is shorter.
- `dsh_browser_wait` waits for a fixed duration. `dsh_browser_wait_for_element` waits for a CSS selector to become visible, hidden, attached, or detached, with a timeout.
- `dsh_browser_snapshot` returns the tab title, URL, visible text, and links. With a `frameId`, the snapshot is read inside that frame and also reports input fields (name box, formula bar), element/canvas rects, the parsed spreadsheet used range when present, and a best-effort grid-cell dump. Frame snapshots mask common `access_token` and `Authorization: Bearer` patterns, including in URLs, but redaction is not comprehensive; other secrets may appear.
- `dsh_browser_find` searches the main page DOM with CSS or XPath and returns ordered candidates with text, links, visibility, and viewport locations. Use it to distinguish repeated matches before clicking.
- `dsh_browser_get_source` returns the original main-document content retained by Chrome, if available. It does not refetch the page or fall back to the live DOM.
- `dsh_browser_get_html` returns current live DOM HTML, optionally for a CSS-selected element and character limit. It does not fetch the original server response bytes. With a `frameId`, the HTML is read inside that frame.
- `dsh_browser_evaluate` runs JavaScript in the selected page context and returns synchronous values or resolved Promise results. It can read or change page state and send requests as the page; `timeoutMs` is capped at 30 seconds. With a `frameId`, the expression runs inside that frame; MV3 CSP blocks `eval`-style evaluation in frames, so the result reports that clearly instead of returning null.
- `dsh_browser_click` clicks a CSS-selected element or a viewport coordinate, showing the virtual cursor sweeping to the point first.
- `dsh_browser_mouse_move` hovers a unique CSS-selected element or moves to viewport coordinates, showing the virtual cursor and dispatching a real `mouseMoved`.
- `dsh_browser_drag` performs a real left-button drag between two visible elements or viewport coordinates, with intermediate mouse-move events. Activate the target tab first; mouse movement can stall on background tabs.
- `dsh_browser_scroll` brings a CSS-selected element into the viewport or scrolls the page by horizontal and vertical deltas. Selector clicks also scroll their target into view automatically.
- `dsh_browser_fill` replaces the text in a CSS-selected field by typing it character by character. `dsh_browser_type_human` does the same into the focused or a CSS-selected field and types the entire supplied string in one run (up to 2000 characters). Bulk pasting-style insertion is not available: instant text injection is a banned action, so `page.type` refuses to run.
- `dsh_browser_submit` submits a CSS-selected form with `requestSubmit()`, preserving native validation. Its result reports whether submission was attempted and the form's validity, not whether the site completed the submission.
- `dsh_browser_keypress` presses a supported key, optionally with modifiers as a chord joined by `+` (e.g. `Ctrl+L`, `Control+Shift+ArrowRight`, `Cmd+A`). Chords that close the browser or tab (`Alt+F4`, `Ctrl+W`, `Cmd+W`, `Ctrl+Shift+Q`) are refused.
- `dsh_browser_screenshot` captures the visible tab and returns it as an image.
- `dsh_browser_sequence` runs up to 25 planned actions on one tab in order, including drag, history navigation, and waits, with a configurable pause between actions (120 ms by default). It returns each step's result and stops at the first failed step.
- `dsh_browser_network` captures request and response metadata from one tab, optionally while running up to 10 planned actions. Sensitive values such as cookies and authorization headers require `includeSensitiveData: true`; request bodies are then included only when Chrome exposes them. Text response bodies require the separate `includeResponseBodies: true` option. Both options can expose credentials or private page data, so keep captures task-scoped. Capture is bounded to 200 requests, 500 cookies for observed URLs, 10 request bodies, and 10 response bodies of at most 256 KB each.
- `dsh_browser_console` captures console messages, browser log entries, and uncaught exceptions for a short period, optionally while planned actions run.
- `dsh_browser_extract` returns bounded structured table rows, links, or list items.
- `dsh_browser_focus`, `dsh_browser_blur`, and `dsh_browser_select` control standard page focus and native select elements. Selection dispatches input and change events but does not submit the form.
- `dsh_browser_upload` attaches user-authorized local files to a file input. The site's change handler may upload immediately; the tool does not submit the form.
- `dsh_browser_download` starts a download, reports its status, or cancels it. Starting defaults to Chrome's Save As dialog. The file lands on the browser's computer.
- `dsh_browser_save_file` fetches a URL from inside a chosen tab, so the request uses that page's cookies and signed-in session, and writes the file into `.tmp/downloads/` under the DSH session workspace. That directory is fixed: the model cannot choose another one, and DSH loads no skills, instructions, or configuration from it. Names DSH reads as instructions (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and their `.local.md` variants) are renamed. The directory and the file are created by processes confined with the DSH sandbox provider (`ctx.sandbox`: bwrap, Landlock, Seatbelt, or Windows ACLs), the file write confined to the download directory alone, so a symlink or directory swapped during the save cannot redirect it. A read-only session policy, or a profile without the working-directory, sandbox-policy, and sandbox services, refuses the save. The bytes travel over the extension's existing connection to DSH; cookies and tokens never leave Chrome, and the model only sees the saved path, size, and SHA-256. Files are limited to 10 MB and never overwrite existing files. When the server answers but the page may not read a cross-origin response (no CORS headers), the user is asked through DSH's approval prompt before the extension's service worker fetches that exact URL with the browser's cookies. That fetch does not follow redirects on its own: each redirect target is shown in a new approval prompt, up to 5 hops. The approval token is a one-time value bound to the tab and URL, exchanged between the plugin and the extension; the model never sees it. Without an approval channel, or under the `never` approval policy, such saves are refused. Network failures are reported, not retried. A save may take up to 3 minutes before it times out.
- `dsh_browser_wait_user` marks a human handoff. The model should tell the user what to do and stop browser actions until the user replies.

For spreadsheet work, use the application's name box to jump to distant cells or ranges, then use keyboard navigation and a sequence of type and keypress actions to enter a row or formula. In Excel Online, commit a cell edit with Enter or the OK button (`#m_excelWebRenderer_ewaCtl_okboxButton`) and abandon it with the cancel button (`#m_excelWebRenderer_ewaCtl_cancelboxButton`); both live in the app frame. To read many cells at once, start `dsh_browser_element_watch` on the formula bar (labelled by the name box), navigate the range, then read the log once. In Google Sheets, the name box and formula bar selectors can change; inspect the current DOM before relying on selectors. Canvas grids (Excel Online, Google Sheets) only render visible cells — scroll the region into view first, and if the data's location is unknown, ask the user where it is. The `chrome-browser` skill includes the full step-by-step spreadsheet guide, including the current Google Sheets selectors.

All live DSH Sessions share the paired browser: operations on the same tab are serialized in order, while different tabs can be driven in parallel. The extension keeps 4 long-polls open (Chrome allows only ~6 connections per host), each answered with a batch of up to 8 queued commands; up to 32 commands execute concurrently and the rest queue FIFO until they run, are cancelled, or the session ends. The host rejects new commands after the 256-command backlog limit. DSH session replay does not restore browser tabs, page contents, or login state.

Clicks, hovers, and drags draw a virtual cursor overlay inside the tab (a closed shadow root using `assets/icons8-select-cursor-16.png`, animated along a Bézier arc, hidden during screenshots). The overlay is cosmetic; real input is dispatched through Chrome's debugger API. Human typing (`dsh_browser_type_human`, `dsh_browser_fill`) sends per-character key events for supported US-layout ASCII, with Unicode text inserted through CDP when required. `delayMs` is a base delay that the configured timing variation adjusts. These settings are an interaction style, not a validated model of human typing or a way to bypass site automation checks. `dsh_browser_fill` rejects tabs and line breaks so replacement text cannot move focus or submit a single-line form.

The extension keeps debugger connections to operated tabs while the DSH browser session is paired. Chrome's debugging notice can change the page viewport on first attach; keeping the connection open prevents the viewport from shifting between inspection and pointer actions. Disconnecting releases those debugger connections; Chrome may leave the notice visible until you dismiss it. If Chrome detaches unexpectedly, take a fresh screenshot or target the element by CSS selector before sending coordinates.

The `chrome-browser` skill is registered with DSH's skill catalog. It teaches the model how to pair, inspect pages, choose tabs, and verify browser actions. If a tool call times out or is cancelled, the host asks the extension to stop the operation; a command already in progress may take a short time to stop.

Tool calls time out after 30 seconds by default. Set `operationTimeoutMs` on the plugin row to adjust the limit:

```yaml
- id: dsh-plugin-chrome-controller
  name: dsh-plugin-chrome-controller
  config:
    operationTimeoutMs: 120000
```

**Raise this before typing long text.** A 333-character message measured with default settings took about 110 to 130 seconds, or roughly 0.35 seconds per character. Treat this as an estimate: the text, random timing, and extension settings affect the result. With the 30-second default, a message longer than about 80 characters may time out partway through. Use `300000` (5 minutes) for ordinary forum or chat messages and `900000` for long ones, then read the field length back and compare it with the intended text. Shortening `baseFlightDelayMs` and the key-hold settings reduces the per-character cost, but no timing profile guarantees site acceptance.

Page content is untrusted and cannot expand or authorize actions beyond the user's request. Use JavaScript evaluation only for the user's task, and do not execute code copied from a page unless requested. The `chrome-browser` skill includes JSON call examples and an inspect-act-verify workflow. The Chrome `debugger` permission gives the extension broad control of browser tabs and Chrome displays its permission warning when the extension is loaded. Screenshots are attached as images when the DSH profile has image attachment support.

## License
